title.zh: 卷一百二十五 列傳第五十 蘇張
title.raw: 卷一百二十五 列傳第五十 蘇張 Volume 125 Biographies 50: Su, Zhang

meta.sourceNote: Body replaced from Wikisource raw text after ChineseNotes scrape due to glyph/encoding artifacts.

sentences.zh: 蘇瓌，字昌容，雍州武功人，隋尚書僕射威之曾孫。

translations.literal: Su Gui, styled Changrong, a native of Wugong in Yong Prefecture, was the great-grandson of Su Wei, Minister of the Left of the Sui.
translations.idiomatic: Su Gui, whose style name was Changrong, came from Wugong in Yong Prefecture. He was the great-grandson of Su Wei, who had served the Sui as Minister of the Left.

sentences.zh: 擢進士第，補恒州參軍。

translations.literal: He was advanced in the jinshi examination and appointed military aide in Heng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After passing the jinshi examination, he was appointed military aide in Heng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 居母喪，哀毀加人，左庶子張大安表舉孝悌，擢豫王府錄事參軍，歷朗、歙二州刺史。

translations.literal: When he dwelt in mourning for his mother, his grief and emaciation exceeded others; Left Guardian of the Heir Zhang Da'an memorialized his filial piety and brotherly conduct; he was advanced to recorder of the Prince of Yu's household and served as prefect of Lang and She.
translations.idiomatic: During mourning for his mother, his grief was so severe that it surpassed others'. Zhang Da'an, Guardian of the Left of the Heir Apparent, recommended him for filial piety and brotherly conduct. He was promoted to recorder of the Prince of Yu's household and later served as prefect of Lang and She.

sentences.zh: 時來俊臣貶州參軍，人懼復用，多致書請瓌，瓌叱其使曰：「吾忝州牧，高下自有體，能過待小人乎？」

translations.literal: At that time Lai Junchen was demoted to prefectural military aide; people feared he would be reused and many sent letters asking Su Gui; Su Gui rebuked the messenger, saying: "I am ashamed to hold the post of prefect—rank has its propriety—can I go out of my way to wait on a petty man?"
translations.idiomatic: When Lai Junchen was demoted to a prefectural aide, many feared he would be restored to power and wrote to Su Gui asking him to intercede. Su Gui scolded the messenger: "I am unworthy to govern this prefecture, but rank still has its propriety. Should I go out of my way to court a petty man?"

sentences.zh: 遂不發書。

translations.literal: He therefore did not send the letter.
translations.idiomatic: He refused to forward the letters.

sentences.zh: 俊臣未至追還，恨之。

translations.literal: Lai Junchen, before he had arrived, was recalled; he bore hatred toward Su Gui.
translations.idiomatic: Lai Junchen was recalled before he even reached his post and came to hate Su Gui for it.

sentences.zh: 由是連外徙，不得入。

translations.literal: Because of this he was repeatedly transferred outward and could not enter the capital.
translations.idiomatic: For this reason Su Gui was transferred from post to post in the provinces and was kept from returning to court.

sentences.zh: 久之，轉揚州大都督府長史。

translations.literal: After a long time he was transferred to senior administrator of the Yangzhou metropolitan prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After some years he was appointed senior administrator of the Yangzhou metropolitan prefecture.

sentences.zh: 州據都會，多名珍怪產，前長史張潛、於辯機貲取鉅萬，瓌單身襆被自將。

translations.literal: The prefecture lay at a great metropolis with many rare and curious products; the previous senior administrators Zhang Qian and Yu Bianji amassed tens of thousands; Su Gui went alone with a bundle wrapped in cloth.
translations.idiomatic: Yangzhou stood at a great commercial hub and produced many rare goods. His predecessors Zhang Qian and Yu Bianji had amassed fortunes in the tens of thousands, but Su Gui traveled alone with nothing but a cloth bundle on his back.

sentences.zh: 徙同州刺史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to prefect of Tong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was then transferred to serve as prefect of Tong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 歳旱，兵當番上者不能赴。

translations.literal: In a year of drought, soldiers due for rotation to garrison duty could not report.
translations.idiomatic: During a drought year, soldiers scheduled for garrison rotation could not afford to report for duty.

sentences.zh: 瓌奏：「宿衛不可闕，宜月賜增半糧，俾相給足，則不闕番。

translations.literal: Su Gui memorialized: "Palace guards cannot be short; monthly rations should be increased by half so they can support one another, and then rotation will not fail.
translations.idiomatic: Su Gui submitted a memorial: "The palace guard cannot be left understaffed. Their monthly grain ration should be increased by half so they can support one another, and garrison rotations will no longer fall short.

sentences.zh: 又宜卻進獻，罷營造不急者。」

translations.literal: Also tribute presented to the court should be reduced and non-urgent construction halted."
translations.idiomatic: Court tribute should also be curtailed, and construction projects that are not urgent should be suspended."

sentences.zh: 不見省。

translations.literal: His advice was not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: The court took no notice.

sentences.zh: 時十道使括天下亡戸，初不立籍，人畏搜括，即流入比縣旁州，更相庾蔽。

translations.literal: At that time commissioners of the ten circuits were tallying fugitive households throughout the realm; initially no registers were established; people feared the search and concealment, and they flowed into neighboring counties of adjacent prefectures, mutually covering for one another.
translations.idiomatic: At that time commissioners for the ten circuits were scouring the empire for unregistered households. Because no proper registers had been set up, people feared the dragnet and fled into neighboring counties and prefectures, where officials shielded one another's concealment.

sentences.zh: 瓌請罷十道使，專責州縣，豫立簿註，天下同日閱正，盡一月止，使柅奸匿，歳一括實，檢制租調，以免勞弊。

translations.literal: Su Gui asked to abolish the ten-circuit commissioners and charge prefectures and counties exclusively, pre-establish register notes, conduct a nationwide review on a single day and complete it within one month, restrain fraud and concealment, conduct one real tally per year, and control land tax and corvée labor to avoid exhaustion of the people.
translations.idiomatic: Su Gui proposed abolishing the ten-circuit commissioners and entrusting prefectures and counties alone with the task. Registers should be prepared in advance, the entire empire reviewed on a single appointed day, and the work finished within one month. That would check fraud and concealment, allow one thorough annual tally, and regulate land tax and corvée without exhausting the populace.

sentences.zh: 武后鑄浮屠，立廟塔，役無虛歳。

translations.literal: Empress Wu cast Buddhas, erected temples and pagodas, and corvée labor had no idle year.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu had Buddha images cast, temples and pagodas built, and corvée labor knew no idle year.

sentences.zh: 瓌以爲「縻損浩廣，雖不出國用，要自民產日殫。

translations.literal: Su Gui held that "the drain is vast and wide; though it does not come from state funds, still the people's production daily dwindles.
translations.idiomatic: Su Gui argued that "the waste is enormous. Even if it does not draw on the state treasury, the people's livelihood is being depleted day by day.

sentences.zh: 百姓不足，君孰與足？

translations.literal: When the common people lack sufficiency, with what will the ruler have sufficiency?
translations.idiomatic: If the people are destitute, how can the ruler be secure in abundance?

sentences.zh: 天下僧尼濫僞相半，請並寺，著僧常員數，缺則補。」

translations.literal: Monks and nuns throughout the realm are half false in excess; I ask to merge monasteries, fix the regular quota of monks, and fill vacancies when there are shortages."
translations.idiomatic: Half the monks and nuns in the realm are fraudulent. I ask that monasteries be consolidated, a fixed quota of clergy established, and vacancies filled only as needed."

sentences.zh: 後善其言。

translations.literal: Later she approved his words.
translations.idiomatic: The empress later came to approve his advice.

sentences.zh: 神龍初，入爲尚書右丞，封懷縣男。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Shenlong era he entered the capital as Right Vice Minister of the Board of Works and was enfeoffed as Baron of Huai County.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Shenlong reign he entered the capital as Right Vice Minister of the Board of Works and was enfeoffed as Baron of Huai County.

sentences.zh: 瓌明曉法令，多識臺省舊章，一朝格式，皆所刪正。

translations.literal: Su Gui was clear in laws and decrees and knew many old regulations of the Secretariat and Chancellery; all formats of the dynasty were edited and corrected by him.
translations.idiomatic: Su Gui was expert in law and familiar with the old regulations of the Secretariat and Chancellery. The administrative formats of the court were largely revised and corrected under his hand.

sentences.zh: 再遷戸部尚書，拜侍中，留守京師。

translations.literal: He was again promoted to Minister of Revenue, appointed Attendant-in-Ordinary, and left to guard the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted again to Minister of Revenue, appointed Attendant-in-Ordinary, and left behind to guard the capital.

sentences.zh: 中宗復政，鄭普思以妖幻位秘書員外監，支黨遍岐、隴間，相煽訹爲亂。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhongzong restored rule, Zheng Pusi held the post of Supernumerary Director of the Secretariat through sorcery and illusion; his partisans spread through Qi and Long, mutually inciting sedition and rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Zhongzong regained power, Zheng Pusi held a post in the Secretariat through sorcery and illusion. His followers spread through the Qi and Long regions, inciting one another to rebellion.

sentences.zh: 瓌捕系普思窮訊，普思妻以左道得幸韋后，出入禁中，有詔勿治。

translations.literal: Su Gui arrested and imprisoned Pusi and interrogated him thoroughly; Pusi's wife, through heterodox ways, had gained favor with Empress Wei and came and went within the inner palace; there was an edict not to prosecute.
translations.idiomatic: Su Gui arrested Zheng Pusi and interrogated him exhaustively. Pusi's wife had won Empress Wei's favor through sorcery and moved freely within the inner palace. An edict was issued ordering that the case not be pursued.

sentences.zh: 瓌廷爭不可，帝猶依違。

translations.literal: Su Gui argued in court that it could not be allowed; the emperor still wavered.
translations.idiomatic: Su Gui argued in open court that this could not stand, but the emperor still hesitated.

sentences.zh: 司直範獻忠，瓌使按普思者，進曰：「瓌爲大臣，不能前誅逆豎而報天子，罪大矣，臣請先斬瓌。」

translations.literal: Director of Scrutiny Fan Xianzhong, whom Su Gui had sent to investigate Pusi, advanced and said: "Su Gui as a great minister could not first execute the rebellious villain and report to the Son of Heaven—the crime is grave; I ask to behead Su Gui first."
translations.idiomatic: Fan Xianzhong, Director of Scrutiny, whom Su Gui had assigned to investigate Pusi, stepped forward and said: "As a chief minister, Su Gui failed to execute this traitor and report to the Son of Heaven. His offense is grave. I ask that Su Gui be beheaded first."

sentences.zh: 於是，僕射魏元忠頓首曰：「瓌長者，用刑不枉，普思法當死。」

translations.literal: Thereupon Left Vice Minister Wei Yuanzhong bowed his head and said: "Su Gui is a man of integrity; in applying punishment he is not unjust—Pusi by law should die."
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Vice Minister Wei Yuanzhong kowtowed and said: "Su Gui is a man of integrity who applies punishment without injustice. By law, Pusi deserves death."

sentences.zh: 帝不得已，流普思於儋州，餘黨論死。

translations.literal: The emperor had no choice; Pusi was banished to Dan Prefecture and the rest of his partisans were sentenced to death.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, left with no alternative, banished Pusi to Dan Prefecture and sentenced his followers to death.

sentences.zh: 累拜尚書右僕射、同中書門下三品，進封許國公。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly appointed Right Vice Minister of the Board of Works, made Grand Counselor with the Chancellery, and advanced in enfeoffment to Duke of Xu.
translations.idiomatic: He was successively appointed Right Vice Minister of the Board of Works and Grand Counselor with the Chancellery, and was advanced in rank to Duke of Xu.

sentences.zh: 帝南郊，國子祭酒祝欽明建白皇后爲亞獻，安樂公主爲終獻。

translations.literal: When the emperor performed the southern suburban sacrifice, Director of the National University Zhu Qinming proposed that the empress be secondary offerer and Princess Anle the final offerer.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor performed the southern suburban sacrifice, Zhu Qinming, Director of the National University, proposed that the empress serve as secondary offerer and Princess Anle as final offerer.

sentences.zh: 瓌以爲非禮，帝前折愧之。

translations.literal: Su Gui held that this was contrary to ritual and before the emperor rebuked and shamed him.
translations.idiomatic: Su Gui judged this contrary to ritual and rebuked Zhu Qinming to his face before the emperor.

sentences.zh: 帝昏懦，不能從。

translations.literal: The emperor was muddled and weak and could not follow his advice.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was muddled and weak-willed and would not heed him.

sentences.zh: 時大臣初拜官，獻食天子，名曰「燒尾」，瓌獨不進。

translations.literal: At that time when great ministers were first appointed they presented food to the Son of Heaven, called "burning the tail"; Su Gui alone did not present it.
translations.idiomatic: At that time newly appointed chief ministers would present food to the emperor in a ceremony called "burning the tail." Su Gui alone refused to do so.

sentences.zh: 及侍宴，宗晉卿嘲之，帝默然。

translations.literal: When he attended a banquet, Zong Jinqing mocked him; the emperor was silent.
translations.idiomatic: At a banquet Zong Jinqing mocked him, and the emperor said nothing.

sentences.zh: 瓌自解於帝曰：「宰相燮和陰陽，代天治物。

translations.literal: Su Gui explained himself to the emperor, saying: "The chief minister harmonizes yin and yang and on Heaven's behalf governs all things.
translations.idiomatic: Su Gui explained himself to the emperor: "A chief minister harmonizes yin and yang and governs the realm on Heaven's behalf.

sentences.zh: 今粒食踴貴，百姓不足，衛兵至三日不食，臣誠不稱職，不敢燒尾。」

translations.literal: Now grain is soaring in price, the common people lack sufficiency, and palace guards have gone three days without food—I truly am unfit for my post and dare not burn the tail."
translations.idiomatic: Grain prices are soaring, the people are destitute, and palace guards have gone three days without food. I am plainly unfit for my office and dare not perform the 'burning the tail' ceremony."

sentences.zh: 帝崩，遺詔皇太后臨朝，相王以太尉輔政。

translations.literal: The emperor died; the testamentary edict had the Empress Dowager preside over court, and the Prince of Xiang as Grand Marshal assist in government.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor died, his testamentary edict placed the Empress Dowager in charge of court affairs and named the Prince of Xiang, as Grand Marshal, to assist in government.

sentences.zh: 後召宰相韋安石、韋巨源、蕭至忠、宗楚客、紀處訥、韋溫、李嶠、韋嗣立、唐休璟、趙彥昭洎瓌議禁中。

translations.literal: Later the empress summoned Chief Ministers Wei Anshi, Wei Juyuan, Xiao Zhizhong, Zong Chuke, Ji Chune, Wei Wen, Li Jiao, Wei Sili, Tang Xiujing, Zhao Yanzhao, and Su Gui to deliberate within the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: The empress then summoned the chief ministers Wei Anshi, Wei Juyuan, Xiao Zhizhong, Zong Chuke, Ji Chune, Wei Wen, Li Jiao, Wei Sili, Tang Xiujing, Zhao Yanzhao, and Su Gui to deliberate within the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 楚客猥曰：「太后臨朝，相王有不通問之嫌，不宜輔政。」

translations.literal: Chuke rudely said: "With the Empress Dowager presiding over court, the Prince of Xiang has the suspicion of failing to inquire after her welfare and should not assist in government."
translations.idiomatic: Chuke said crudely: "With the Empress Dowager presiding over court, the Prince of Xiang is open to suspicion for failing to pay his respects and should not assist in government."

sentences.zh: 瓌正色曰：「遺制乃先帝意，安得輒改？」

translations.literal: Su Gui with stern countenance said: "The testamentary institution was the late emperor's intent—how can it be rashly altered?"
translations.idiomatic: Su Gui said sternly: "The testamentary arrangement was the late emperor's intent. How can it be altered at will?"

sentences.zh: 楚客等恕，卒削相王輔政事，瓌稱疾不朝。

translations.literal: Chuke and the others were resentful; in the end they stripped the Prince of Xiang of his role assisting in government, and Su Gui claimed illness and did not attend court.
translations.idiomatic: Chuke and his allies were resentful. In the end they stripped the Prince of Xiang of his role in government, and Su Gui pleaded illness and stopped attending court.

sentences.zh: 是月，韋氏敗，睿宗即位，進左僕射。

translations.literal: That month the Wei clan was destroyed; Emperor Ruizong took the throne, and Su Gui was advanced to Left Vice Minister.
translations.idiomatic: That month the Wei faction was overthrown. When Emperor Ruizong took the throne, Su Gui was promoted to Left Vice Minister.

sentences.zh: 景雲元年，老病，罷爲太子少傅。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingyun, old and ill, he was dismissed and made Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Jingyun era, aged and ill, he was relieved of office and appointed Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十二，贈司空荊州大都督，謚曰文貞。

translations.literal: He died at age seventy-two; posthumously he was given the office of Minister of Works and metropolitan governor of Jingzhou; his posthumous title was Wenzhen.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of seventy-two. Posthumously he was given the title Minister of Works and metropolitan governor of Jingzhou, with the posthumous name Wenzhen.

sentences.zh: 皇太子別次發哀。

translations.literal: The Crown Prince held mourning at a separate station.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince held mourning rites at a separate pavilion.

sentences.zh: 遺令薄葬，布車一乘。

translations.literal: His testamentary order was for a simple burial and one carriage of cloth.
translations.idiomatic: His testamentary instructions called for a simple burial and a single cloth-covered carriage.

sentences.zh: 瓌治州考課常最，爲宰相，陳當世病利甚多。

translations.literal: In governing prefectures Su Gui's performance evaluations were constantly highest; as chief minister he set forth many current ills and benefits.
translations.idiomatic: In governing prefectures Su Gui's performance evaluations were consistently the highest. As chief minister he identified many of the era's abuses and proposed remedies.

sentences.zh: 韋溫始爲汴洲司倉參軍，以賕被杖，及用事，憚瓌正，卒不敢傷。

translations.literal: Wei Wen had first served as grain-store aide in Bian Prefecture and was beaten for bribery; when he came to power he feared Su Gui's integrity and in the end did not dare harm him.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Wen had once served as grain-store aide in Bian Prefecture and was beaten for taking bribes. When he later rose to power he feared Su Gui's integrity and in the end did not dare harm him.

sentences.zh: 開元二年，賜其家實封百戸，長子頲固辭，乃擢中子乂左補闕。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kaiyuan his family was granted a substantive fief of one hundred households; the eldest son Ting firmly declined, and therefore the second son Yi was advanced to Left Remonstrator.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Kaiyuan his family was granted a substantive fief of one hundred households. His eldest son Ting firmly declined the honor, so his second son Yi was promoted to Left Remonstrator instead.

sentences.zh: 六年，詔與劉幽求配享睿宗廟廷。

translations.literal: In the sixth year an edict had him share sacrifice in Emperor Ruizong's temple hall with Liu Youqiu.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year an edict ordered that he share sacrifice in Emperor Ruizong's temple hall alongside Liu Youqiu.

sentences.zh: 文宗大和中，錄舊德，官其四代孫翔。

translations.literal: In the Dahe era of Emperor Wenzong, recording old merit, his fourth-generation descendant Xiang was given office.
translations.idiomatic: During the Dahe era of Emperor Wenzong, in recognition of his old merit, Su Gui's fourth-generation descendant Xiang was given an official post.

sentences.zh: 瓌諸子，頲、詵顯。

translations.literal: Among Su Gui's sons, Ting and Shen were prominent.
translations.idiomatic: Among Su Gui's sons, Ting and Shen were the most prominent.

sentences.zh: 瓌子 頲頲，字廷碩，弱敏悟，一覽至千言，輒覆誦。

translations.literal: Su Gui's son Ting, styled Tingshuo, was from youth keen and perceptive; with one reading of up to a thousand characters he could recite them back from memory.
translations.idiomatic: Su Gui's son Ting, whose style name was Tingshuo, was from childhood quick and perceptive. After a single reading of as many as a thousand characters he could recite them from memory.

sentences.zh: 第進士，調烏程尉。

translations.literal: He placed in the jinshi examination and was appointed aide in Wucheng.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and was appointed aide in Wucheng.

sentences.zh: 武后封嵩髙，舉賢良方正異等，除左司禦率府冑曹參軍。

translations.literal: When Empress Wu performed the fengshan at Mount Song, he was recommended as outstanding in the erudite and upright category and appointed aide in the Left Bureau of the Imperial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Wu performed the fengshan rite at Mount Song, he was recommended as outstanding in the erudite and upright category and appointed aide in the Left Bureau of the Imperial Guard.

sentences.zh: 吏部侍郎馬載曰：「古稱一日千里，蘇生是已。」

translations.literal: Vice Minister of the Board of Civil Office Ma Zai said: "The ancients spoke of a thousand li in one day—this Su is such a one."
translations.idiomatic: Ma Zai, Vice Minister of the Board of Civil Office, said: "The ancients spoke of traveling a thousand li in a single day. This young Su is such a man."

sentences.zh: 再遷監察御史。

translations.literal: He was again promoted to investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted again to investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 長安中，詔覆來俊臣等冤獄，頲驗發其誣，多從洗宥。

translations.literal: In the Chang'an era an edict ordered review of wrongful cases of Lai Junchen and others; Ting verified and exposed their false accusations, and many were pardoned and released.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chang'an era an edict ordered a review of wrongful cases involving Lai Junchen and others. Ting verified and exposed their false accusations, and many victims were pardoned and released.

sentences.zh: 遷給事中、修文館學士，拜中書舍人。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Supervising Secretary and Academician of the Hall for Cultivating Literature, and appointed Drafting Secretary of the Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Supervising Secretary and Academician of the Hall for Cultivating Literature, then appointed Drafting Secretary of the Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 時瓌同中書門下三品，父子同在禁管，朝廷榮之。

translations.literal: At that time Su Gui was Grand Counselor with the Chancellery; father and son were together within the inner precincts, and the court honored them.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Su Gui served as Grand Counselor with the Chancellery. Father and son held office together within the inner precincts, and the court regarded it as a signal honor.

sentences.zh: 玄宗平内難，書詔塡委，獨頲在太極後筦，口所占授，功狀百緒，輕重無所差。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuanzong quelled the inner turmoil, edicts and proclamations piled up; Ting alone was behind the Hall of Supreme Ultimate, dictating by mouth; merit records ran to hundreds of threads, and in weight and importance there was no error.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuanzong quelled the inner turmoil, edicts and proclamations piled up endlessly. Ting alone worked behind the Hall of Supreme Ultimate, dictating them by word of mouth. Merit records ran to hundreds of items, yet he made no error in weight or importance.

sentences.zh: 書史白曰：「丐公徐之，不然，手腕脱矣。」

translations.literal: The clerk said: "I beg the lord to go slowly, otherwise your wrist will come off."
translations.idiomatic: A clerk said to him: "Please slow down, my lord, or your wrist will give out."

sentences.zh: 中書令李嶠曰：「舍人思若湧泉，吾所不及。」

translations.literal: Chief Minister Li Jiao said: "The Drafting Secretary's thoughts flow like a spring—I cannot match him."
translations.idiomatic: Chief Minister Li Jiao said: "The drafting secretary's thoughts pour forth like a spring. I cannot match him."

sentences.zh: 遷太常少卿，仍知制誥。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and still controlled drafting of edicts.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices while retaining charge of drafting edicts.

sentences.zh: 遭父喪，起爲工部侍郎，辭不拜，終制乃就職。

translations.literal: When his father died he was recalled to serve as Vice Minister of the Board of Works; he declined to accept the appointment and took office only after the mourning period ended.
translations.idiomatic: After his father's death he was recalled to serve as Vice Minister of the Board of Works, but he declined the appointment and took office only after the mourning period ended.

sentences.zh: 帝問宰相：「有自工部侍郎得中書侍郎乎？」

translations.literal: The emperor asked the chief ministers: "Has anyone gone from Vice Minister of the Board of Works to Vice Minister of the Chancellery?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked the chief ministers: "Has anyone ever risen from Vice Minister of the Board of Works to Vice Minister of the Chancellery?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「陛下任賢惟所命，何資之計？」

translations.literal: They replied: "Your Majesty appoints the worthy as you command—what calculation of qualifications is needed?"
translations.idiomatic: They replied: "Your Majesty appoints the worthy as you see fit. What need is there to reckon qualifications?"

sentences.zh: 乃詔以頲爲中書侍郎。

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict appointed Ting Vice Minister of the Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: An edict was then issued appointing Ting Vice Minister of the Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 帝勞曰：「方美官缺，毎欲用卿，然宰相議遂無及者，朕爲卿恨。

translations.literal: The emperor comforted him, saying: "Fine offices are vacant, and I have wished to use you each time, yet in the chief ministers' deliberations there has been no reaching you—I regret this for your sake.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor reassured him: "Fine offices have stood vacant, and each time I have wished to appoint you, yet in the chief ministers' deliberations the matter never reached you. I regret that on your behalf.

sentences.zh: 陸象先歿，紫微侍郎未嘗補，朕思其人無易卿者。」

translations.literal: When Lu Xiangxian died, the Vice Minister of the Palace Secretariat had never been filled—I think of a man and none can replace you."
translations.idiomatic: When Lu Xiangxian died, the post of Vice Minister of the Palace Secretariat went unfilled. I have searched for a replacement, and no one can take your place."

sentences.zh: 頲頓首謝。

translations.literal: Ting bowed his head in thanks.
translations.idiomatic: Ting kowtowed in thanks.

sentences.zh: 明日加知制誥，給政事食，給食自頲始。

translations.literal: The next day he was additionally given charge of drafting edicts and granted food for handling state affairs—granting such food began with Ting.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he was additionally charged with drafting edicts and granted food for handling state affairs—the practice of granting such food began with Ting.

sentences.zh: 時李軿對掌書命，帝曰：「前世李嶠、蘇味道文擅當時，號『蘇李』。

translations.literal: At that time Li Han shared charge of drafting; the emperor said: "In a former age Li Jiao and Su Weidao excelled in literature of their time and were called 'Su and Li'.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Li Han shared charge of drafting documents. The emperor said: "In an earlier age Li Jiao and Su Weidao dominated the literary world and were known as 'Su and Li'.

sentences.zh: 今朕得頲及軿，何愧前人哉！」

translations.literal: Now I have obtained Ting and Han—how can I be ashamed before the men of old!"
translations.idiomatic: Now that I have Ting and Han, how can I feel inferior to those earlier masters!"

sentences.zh: 俄襲封許國公。

translations.literal: Before long he inherited enfeoffment as Duke of Xu.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he inherited his father's enfeoffment as Duke of Xu.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃盜邊，諸將數敗，虜益張，秣騎内侵。

translations.literal: The Tibetans raided the borders; the generals were repeatedly defeated; the enemy grew more arrogant; cavalry fed on fodder and invaded inward.
translations.idiomatic: The Tibetans raided the frontier. Tang generals suffered repeated defeats, the enemy grew bolder, and their cavalry drove deep into Tang territory.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，欲自將兵討之。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry and wished to lead the army in person to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious and wished to lead the army in person against them.

sentences.zh: 頲諫曰：「古稱荒服，取荒忽之義，非常奉職貢也。

translations.literal: Ting remonstrated, saying: "The ancients called them the distant domain, taking the sense of neglect and remoteness—they are not those who regularly present tribute and gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Ting remonstrated: "The ancients called such peoples the distant domain, taking the sense of remoteness and neglect. They are not peoples who regularly present tribute.

sentences.zh: 故來則拒，去則勿逐，以禽獸畜之，羈縻禦之。

translations.literal: Therefore when they come, reject them; when they go, do not pursue—keep them as beasts and birds, control them through loose reins.
translations.idiomatic: When they come, repel them; when they withdraw, do not pursue. Treat them as one would beasts, and govern them through loose reins.

sentences.zh: 譬若獵然，羽毛不入服用，體肉不登郊廟，則王者不射也。

translations.literal: It is like hunting: if feathers do not enter dress and adornment, and flesh does not ascend to the suburban altars, then the king does not shoot.
translations.idiomatic: It is like hunting: if the feathers are unfit for dress and the flesh unfit for the suburban altars, the king does not shoot.

sentences.zh: 況萬乘之重，與犬羊蚊虻語負勝哉？

translations.literal: How much more the weight of the ten-thousand-chariot ruler—should he speak of winning or losing with dogs, sheep, mosquitoes, and gnats?
translations.idiomatic: How much less should the ruler of ten thousand chariots stoop to contest victory with dogs, sheep, mosquitoes, and gnats?

sentences.zh: 遠夷左衽，不足以辱天子，亦可見矣。

translations.literal: Distant barbarians with garments buttoned to the left are not sufficient to humiliate the Son of Heaven—this too can be seen.
translations.idiomatic: Barbarians of the distant border, with garments buttoned to the left, are scarcely fit to humble the Son of Heaven. That much is plain.

sentences.zh: 雖然，兵法先聲後實，陛下姑班親征之詔，而敕虓將謀夫投會濟師，則吐蕃不日崩破，亦無待躬致天討也。

translations.literal: Nevertheless, in military law sound precedes substance; Your Majesty might for the moment promulgate an edict for a personal campaign and order fierce generals and strategists to strike at the opportune moment and bring troops across—then Tibet will before long collapse and break, and there will be no need for Your Majesty personally to deliver Heaven's punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Still, military doctrine holds that reputation must precede force. Your Majesty might promulgate an edict announcing a personal campaign and order your fiercest generals to strike when the moment is ripe and bring troops across the border. Tibet would soon collapse, without Your Majesty needing to deliver Heaven's punishment in person.

sentences.zh: 臣謂岐、隴雕弊積年，若千乘萬騎，供億不涯，誠恐徭役内興，寇掠外虞，斯人不堪，一也。

translations.literal: Your subject holds that Qi and Long have been exhausted for years; if a thousand chariots and ten thousand horsemen are supplied without limit, I truly fear corvée labor will rise within and plundering enemies will threaten without—the people cannot bear it. This is the first point.
translations.idiomatic: I hold that the Qi and Long regions have been exhausted for years. If a thousand chariots and ten thousand horsemen must be supplied without limit, I fear corvée labor will rise within while raiders threaten from without. The people cannot bear it. That is my first objection.

sentences.zh: 戎虜之性，驟往倏來，敗不恥奔，勝不讓成。

translations.literal: The nature of the Rong barbarians is to go suddenly and come suddenly; in defeat they are not ashamed to flee, in victory they do not yield achievement.
translations.idiomatic: The nature of these barbarians is to strike suddenly and withdraw just as quickly. They feel no shame in flight after defeat and concede nothing after victory.

sentences.zh: 若大軍一臨邊，怖震鳥散，彼出多方，我受其誤，二也。

translations.literal: If a great army once reaches the border, they will be terrified and scatter like birds; they will strike from many directions and we will suffer their deception. This is the second point.
translations.idiomatic: If a great army reaches the border, they will scatter in terror like birds. Yet they will strike from many directions and we will fall prey to their stratagems. That is my second objection.

sentences.zh: 太上皇聞陛下身對寇塲，不能無憂，烝烝之思，何以自安？

translations.literal: The Retired Emperor, hearing that Your Majesty will face the enemy in person on the battlefield, cannot be without worry—how can his deep affection find peace? This is the third point.
translations.idiomatic: The Retired Emperor, hearing that Your Majesty will face the enemy in person on the battlefield, cannot help worrying. How can his deep affection for you find peace? That is my third objection.

sentences.zh: 三也。

translations.literal: This is the third point.
translations.idiomatic: Those are my three objections.

sentences.zh: 漢蒯成侯諫髙帝曰：『上嘗自勞，豈謂無人使哉？』

translations.literal: The Marquis of Kuai of Han remonstrated with Emperor Gaozu of Han, saying: "Your Majesty once went in person to comfort the troops—does that mean there is no one to be sent?"
translations.idiomatic: The Marquis of Kuai of Han once remonstrated with Emperor Gaozu, saying: "When Your Majesty went in person to comfort the troops, did that mean there was no one else who could be sent?"

sentences.zh: 髙帝以爲愛我。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu took it as love for himself.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu understood this as an expression of devotion to him.

sentences.zh: 今將相大臣，豈無爲陛下宣力者，何親行之遽邪？」

translations.literal: Now among generals, ministers, and great officials, is there none who will exert strength on Your Majesty's behalf—why go in person so hastily?"
translations.idiomatic: Among your generals, ministers, and great officials, is there truly no one who will exert himself on Your Majesty's behalf? Why rush to go in person?"

sentences.zh: 不省。

translations.literal: He was not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor paid no heed.

sentences.zh: 復上言：「王者之師，有征無戰，藩貢或闕，王命征之，於是乎治兵其郊，獲辭而止，非謂按甲自臨。

translations.literal: He again submitted a memorial: "The army of a true king has campaigns but no battles; when a feudatory's tribute is sometimes lacking, the king's command campaigns against him—thereupon troops are arrayed at the border, and when submission is obtained they stop; this does not mean donning armor and going in person.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted another memorial: "The army of a true king campaigns without fighting. When a vassal's tribute falls short, the king's command goes forth against him. Troops are then arrayed at the border, and when submission is obtained they withdraw. This does not mean the king dons armor and goes in person.

sentences.zh: 敵人畏之莫敢戰也。

translations.literal: The enemy fears it and dares not fight.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy fears it and dares not give battle.

sentences.zh: 古天子無親將，惟黃帝五十二戰，當未平之時。

translations.literal: In antiquity the Son of Heaven did not lead in person; only the Yellow Emperor fought fifty-two battles, when the realm was not yet pacified.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity the Son of Heaven did not lead armies in person. Only the Yellow Emperor fought fifty-two battles—and that was while the realm was not yet pacified.

sentences.zh: 自阪泉功成，則修身閑居，無爲無事。

translations.literal: From the time the achievement at Banquan was complete, he cultivated himself and dwelt at leisure, without action and without affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Once victory was won at Banquan, he cultivated himself in retirement, without action and without affairs.

sentences.zh: 陛下撥定禍亂，方當深視髙居，制禮作樂，禪梁父，登空同，何至厭天居，衽金革，爲一日之敵？

translations.literal: Your Majesty has settled turmoil and disorder and should now look deeply from on high, establish ritual and compose music, perform the fengshan at Mount Liangfu, ascend Mount Kongtong—how reach the point of tiring of the heavenly dwelling, spreading out armor and weapons, and becoming the enemy of a single day?
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has settled turmoil and disorder. You should now look down from on high, establish ritual and compose music, perform the fengshan at Mount Liangfu, and ascend Mount Kongtong. Why grow weary of the heavenly dwelling, take up armor and weapons, and become the enemy of a single day's foe?

sentences.zh: 今吐蕃遣渠領幹犯國令，軍吏一不勝，而陛下屈至尊爲之敵，雖朝鼎夕砧，猶未可以誇四夷，安足勞聖躬哉？

translations.literal: Now Tibet sends its leaders to violate the state's commands; the army officers once fail to win—and Your Majesty bends the supreme honor to become their enemy; even if morning is cauldron and evening is chopping block, still it cannot be used to boast to the four barbarians—how can it suffice to weary the sacred person?
translations.idiomatic: Now Tibet sends its leaders to violate our laws. Because a single officer fails to win, Your Majesty would bend the supreme dignity to become their enemy. Even if you fought from dawn to dusk, you could not boast to the four barbarians. How can that justify exhausting the sacred person?

sentences.zh: 虜之入，唯盜羊馬，發窖裭衣，未嘗殺略邊人，其罪易原也。

translations.literal: When the barbarians enter, they only steal sheep and horses, open cellars and take stored clothing—they have never slaughtered and plundered border people; their crime is easy to pardon.
translations.idiomatic: When they raid, the Tibetans steal only sheep and horses and plunder stored goods from cellars. They have never slaughtered border populations, and their offenses are easily forgiven.

sentences.zh: 臣恐虜情狼顧，牽連北狄，聞六師之行，入幽、并，犯靈、夏，南動京師，太上皇一致憂勞，是陛下以天下之安，不能寧其親也。

translations.literal: Your subject fears the barbarians' nature of looking back like wolves, drawing in the northern Di; hearing of the march of the six armies, they will enter You and Bing, violate Ling and Xia, stir the south toward the capital—the Retired Emperor will share worry and toil; this is Your Majesty using the peace of the realm and yet unable to give peace to your parent.
translations.idiomatic: I fear the Tibetans, wolflike in their caution, may draw in the northern tribes. Hearing that the six armies are marching, they may invade You and Bing, strike at Ling and Xia, and threaten the capital. The Retired Emperor would share in the worry and toil. Your Majesty would sacrifice the peace of the realm yet fail to secure peace for your own father.

sentences.zh: 臣固曰，居中制勝，策之上者。

translations.literal: Your subject has always said that holding the center and controlling victory from there is the highest strategy.
translations.idiomatic: I have always held that holding the center and controlling victory from there is the highest strategy.

sentences.zh: 若夫擇良將，募重而約嚴，違律必誅，殺敵必賞，多出金以購酋長，虜亡無日矣。

translations.literal: As for selecting good generals, recruiting heavily with strict covenants, punishing those who violate regulations, rewarding those who kill the enemy, and spending much gold to buy off chieftains—the barbarians will perish before long.
translations.idiomatic: Select capable generals, recruit troops generously under strict discipline, punish every violation of regulations, reward every enemy killed, and spend gold liberally to buy off chieftains—the Tibetans would soon be destroyed.

sentences.zh: 願稍遷延，以須西音。」

translations.literal: I wish Your Majesty to delay slightly and wait for news from the west."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that Your Majesty delay slightly and await news from the western front."

sentences.zh: 亦會薛訥大破吐蕃，俘獲不貲，由是帝止不行。

translations.literal: It also happened that Xue Ne inflicted a great defeat on Tibet, with captives and booty beyond counting; because of this the emperor stopped and did not go.
translations.idiomatic: It happened at the same time that Xue Ne inflicted a crushing defeat on Tibet, taking captives and booty beyond counting. For this reason the emperor abandoned his plan to march in person.

sentences.zh: 時詔立靖陵碑，命頲爲之詞，辭曰：「前世帝後不誌碑，事弗稽古，謂之不法。

translations.literal: At that time an edict ordered the erection of a stele at Jing Mausoleum and commanded Ting to compose its text; he declined, saying: "In former ages emperors and empresses did not inscribe steles—affairs not examined against antiquity are called contrary to law.
translations.idiomatic: An edict was issued to erect a stele at Jing Mausoleum and Ting was ordered to compose its inscription. He declined, saying: "In former ages emperors and empresses did not inscribe steles. Affairs that fail to follow antiquity are called unlawful.

sentences.zh: 審當可者，祖宗諸陵，一須營立，後嗣謂何？」

translations.literal: If it is truly permissible, then all the mausoleums of the ancestors must be provided for—what will later generations say?"
translations.idiomatic: If this practice is truly permissible, then steles must be erected at all the ancestral tombs. What will later generations say?"

sentences.zh: 帝不納其言。

translations.literal: The emperor did not accept his words.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not accept his advice.

sentences.zh: 開元四年，進同紫微黃門平章事，修國史，與宋璟同當國。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Kaiyuan he was advanced to Grand Counselor with the Palace Secretariat and Chancellery, edited the national history, and together with Song Jing shared charge of the state.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Kaiyuan he was promoted to Grand Counselor with the Palace Secretariat and Chancellery, charged with editing the national history, and shared governance of the state with Song Jing.

sentences.zh: 璟剛正，多所裁決，頲能推其長。

translations.literal: Jing was stern and upright and made many decisions; Ting was able to extend his strengths.
translations.idiomatic: Jing was stern and upright and made many firm decisions. Ting was able to extend and complement his strengths.

sentences.zh: 在帝前敷奏，璟有未及，或少屈，頲輒助成之，有不會意，頲更申璟所執，故帝未嘗不從，二人相得歡甚。

translations.literal: When presenting matters before the emperor, if Jing had not reached some point or was slightly yielding, Ting would help complete it; if the emperor did not understand, Ting would further state what Jing held—therefore the emperor never failed to follow, and the two men got on together with great pleasure.
translations.idiomatic: When presenting matters before the emperor, if Jing had not fully stated his case or yielded slightly, Ting would help complete the argument. If the emperor did not understand, Ting would restate Jing's position. The emperor never failed to follow their counsel, and the two men worked together in great harmony.

sentences.zh: 璟嘗曰：「吾與蘇氏父子同爲宰相，僕射長厚，自是國器；

translations.literal: Jing once said: "I and the Su father and son have together served as chief ministers; the Vice Minister is long in virtue and generous—he is by nature a pillar of the state;
translations.idiomatic: Jing once said: "The Su father and son and I have served together as chief ministers. The father was long in virtue and generous—he was by nature a pillar of the state.

sentences.zh: 若獻可替否，事至即斷，盡公不顧私，則今丞相爲過之。」

translations.literal: if in offering what is acceptable and replacing what is not, when affairs arrive deciding at once, exhausting public duty without regard to private interest, then the present chief minister surpasses him."
translations.idiomatic: But in offering what is acceptable and replacing what is not, in deciding affairs as they arise, and in exhausting public duty without regard to private interest, the present chief minister surpasses him."

sentences.zh: 八年，罷爲禮部尚書。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was dismissed and made Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was relieved of office and appointed Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 俄檢校益州大都督長史，按察節度劍南諸州。

translations.literal: Before long he was made acting senior administrator of the Yi metropolitan prefecture and inspected and regulated the prefectures of Jiannan.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was appointed acting senior administrator of the Yi metropolitan prefecture with authority to inspect and regulate the prefectures of Jiannan.

sentences.zh: 時蜀彫τ，人流亡，詔頲收劍南山澤鹽鐵自贍。

translations.literal: At that time Shu was exhausted and depleted, and the people were fleeing; an edict commanded Ting to collect the salt and iron of the mountains and marshes of Jiannan to support himself.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Shu was exhausted and depleted, and the people were fleeing. An edict commanded Ting to collect revenue from the salt and iron of Jiannan's mountains and marshes to support local administration.

sentences.zh: 頲尚簡靜，重興力役，即募戌人，輸雇直，開井置爐，量入計出，分所贏市谷，以廣見糧。

translations.literal: Ting valued simplicity and quiet; he emphasized reviving corvée labor, immediately recruiting garrison soldiers, paying hire wages, opening wells and setting up furnaces, measuring income and calculating expenditure, dividing profits to buy grain, and thereby expanding visible grain stores.
translations.idiomatic: Ting valued simplicity and restraint. He revived corvée projects, recruited garrison soldiers and paid them wages, opened wells and set up salt furnaces, balanced income against expenditure, and used the profits to buy grain and expand local grain reserves.

sentences.zh: 時前司馬皇甫恂使蜀，檄取庫錢市錦半臂、琵琶捍撥、玲瓏鞭，頲不肯予，因上言：「遣使銜命，先取不急，非陛下以山澤贍軍費意。」

translations.literal: At that time the former military aide Huangfu Xun was sent to Shu and by dispatch took treasury funds to buy brocade half-sleeves, pipa plectrums, and exquisitely wrought whips; Ting refused to give them and therefore submitted a memorial: "Sending envoys bearing commands to take first what is not urgent is not Your Majesty's intent in using mountains and marshes to support military expenses."
translations.idiomatic: Huangfu Xun, formerly military aide, was sent to Shu and by official dispatch took treasury funds to buy brocade vests, pipa plectrums, and ornamental whips. Ting refused to provide the funds and memorialized: "When envoys bearing imperial commands take what is not urgent first, that is not Your Majesty's intent in using mountain and marsh revenues to support military expenses."

sentences.zh: 或謂頲：「公在遠，叵得忤上意。」

translations.literal: Some told Ting: "You are far away—how can you go against the emperor's intent?"
translations.idiomatic: Some told Ting: "You are far from court. How can you defy the emperor's intent?"

sentences.zh: 頲曰：「不然。

translations.literal: Ting said: "Not so.
translations.idiomatic: Ting replied: "Not so.

sentences.zh: 明主不以私愛奪至公，吾可以遠近廢忠臣節邪？」

translations.literal: A enlightened ruler does not let private affection seize supreme public duty—can I because of distance near or far abandon the integrity of a loyal minister?"
translations.idiomatic: An enlightened ruler does not let private affection override supreme public duty. How can I, merely because I am far from court, abandon the integrity of a loyal minister?"

sentences.zh: 巂州蠻苴院與吐蕃連謀入寇，獲諜者，吏請討之，頲不聽，移書還其諜曰：「毋得爾。」

translations.literal: The barbarian Juyuan of Xi Prefecture conspired with Tibet to invade; when a spy was captured, officials asked to attack them; Ting did not listen and sent a letter returning their spy, saying: "You must not do this."
translations.idiomatic: The Juyuan tribe of Xi Prefecture conspired with Tibet to invade. When a spy was captured, officials asked permission to attack. Ting refused and sent a letter returning the spy: "You must not do this again."

sentences.zh: 苴院羞悔，不敢侵邊。

translations.literal: Juyuan was ashamed and repentant and did not dare invade the border.
translations.idiomatic: The Juyuan were ashamed and repentant and did not dare raid the border again.

sentences.zh: 從封泰山，詔頌朝覲壇，世咨其文。

translations.literal: He followed the fengshan at Mount Tai; an edict had him compose the text for the Court Audience Altar, and the age praised his writing.
translations.idiomatic: He accompanied the emperor to the fengshan at Mount Tai. An edict commanded him to compose the text for the Court Audience Altar, and contemporaries praised his prose.

sentences.zh: 還，分主十銓事。

translations.literal: On his return he was assigned to share charge of the ten selection boards.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was assigned to share charge of the ten selection boards for official appointments.

sentences.zh: 卒，年五十八。

translations.literal: He died at age fifty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of fifty-eight.

sentences.zh: 帝猶視朝，起居舍人韋述上疎曰：「貞觀、永徽時，大臣薨，輒置朝舉哀，成終始恩，上有旌賢録舊之德，下有生榮死哀之美。

translations.literal: The emperor was still holding court; Attendant Recorder Wei Shu submitted a memorial saying: "In the Zhenguan and Yonghui eras, when great ministers died, court was suspended for mourning—this completes the grace of beginning and end; above there is the virtue of honoring the worthy and recording the old; below there is the beauty of glory in life and mourning in death.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was still holding court when Attendant Recorder Wei Shu submitted a memorial: "In the Zhenguan and Yonghui eras, when great ministers died, court was suspended for mourning. This completes the grace owed from beginning to end. Above, it displays the virtue of honoring the worthy and remembering the old. Below, it embodies the beauty of glory in life and mourning in death.

sentences.zh: 昔晉知悼子卒，平公宴樂，杜蕢一言而悟，《春秋》載之。

translations.literal: In former times when Zhi Daozi of Jin died, Duke Ping feasted and made music; Du Kui with one word made him understand, and the Spring and Autumn Annals records it.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhi Daozi of Jin died, Duke Ping continued to feast and make music until Du Kui spoke one word and made him understand. The Spring and Autumn Annals records this.

sentences.zh: 故禮部尚書頲累葉輔弼，奉事軒陛二十餘年，今奄忽不還，邦人痛嗟。

translations.literal: Therefore Minister of Rites Ting for generations served as chief minister, attending at the imperial throne for more than twenty years; now suddenly he does not return, and the people of the state grieve and sigh.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Rites Ting came from generations of chief ministers and served at the imperial throne for more than twenty years. Now he has suddenly departed, and the realm grieves.

sentences.zh: 惟帷盡之舊，股肱之戚，宜即廢朝，明君臣之誼。」

translations.literal: As one who shared the curtain to the end and was a limb-and-thigh kin, he should immediately have court suspended to clarify the bond between ruler and minister."
translations.idiomatic: As one who shared the imperial curtain to the end and served as the emperor's right hand, court should immediately be suspended to clarify the bond between ruler and minister."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「固朕意也。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "This has always been my intent."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "That has always been my intent."

sentences.zh: 即日帳次哭洛城南門，不朝。

translations.literal: That same day he set up a mourning tent and wept at the south gate of Luoyang and did not hold court.
translations.idiomatic: That same day he set up a mourning tent and wept at the south gate of Luoyang, and court was suspended.

sentences.zh: 詔贈右丞相，謚曰文憲。

translations.literal: An edict posthumously gave him Right Chief Minister and the posthumous title Wenzian.
translations.idiomatic: An edict posthumously appointed him Right Chief Minister with the posthumous name Wenzian.

sentences.zh: 葬日，帝遊咸宜宮，將獵，聞之，曰：「頲且葬，我忍自娯哉！」

translations.literal: On the day of burial the emperor was visiting Xianyi Palace and was about to go hunting; hearing of it he said: "Ting is about to be buried—how can I bear to amuse myself!"
translations.idiomatic: On the day of burial the emperor was visiting Xianyi Palace and was about to go hunting. When he heard the news he said: "Ting is being buried today. How can I bear to amuse myself!"

sentences.zh: 半道而還。

translations.literal: He turned back halfway.
translations.idiomatic: He turned back halfway.

sentences.zh: 頲性廉儉，奉稟悉推散諸弟親族，儲無長貲。

translations.literal: Ting's nature was frugal and simple; his salary and grain allowance he entirely distributed among his younger brothers and kin, and he stored no lasting wealth.
translations.idiomatic: Ting was frugal by nature. He distributed his salary and grain allowance entirely among his younger brothers and kin, and left no lasting wealth in store.

sentences.zh: 自景龍後，與張説以文章顯，稱望略等，故時號「燕許大手筆」。

translations.literal: From after the Jinglong era he and Zhang Yue were prominent through literature; their reputation was roughly equal, and therefore the age called them "the great brush of Yan and Xu."
translations.idiomatic: From the Jinglong era onward he and Zhang Yue rose to prominence through their literary skill. Their reputations were roughly equal, and contemporaries called them "the great brush of Yan and Xu."

sentences.zh: 帝愛其文，曰：「卿所爲詔令，別録副本，署臣某撰，朕當留中。」

translations.literal: The emperor loved his writing and said: "The edicts and commands you compose—make a separate copy, sign it 'composed by your minister so-and-so,' and I shall keep it within the palace."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor admired his prose and said: "For every edict and command you compose, make a separate copy, sign it as composed by your minister, and I shall keep it within the palace archives."

sentences.zh: 後遂爲故事。

translations.literal: This later became established precedent.
translations.idiomatic: This later became established precedent.

sentences.zh: 其後李德裕著論曰「近世詔誥，惟頲敘事外自爲文章」云。

translations.literal: Later Li Deyu wrote in a treatise: "In recent times of edicts and proclamations, only Ting beyond narrating affairs made literature of his own," and so on.
translations.idiomatic: Later Li Deyu wrote in a treatise that "among recent edicts and proclamations, only Ting's went beyond mere narration to become literature in their own right."

sentences.zh: 瓌子 詵詵，字廷言，舉賢良方正高第，補汾陰尉，遷秘書詳正學士，累轉給事中，時頲爲紫微侍郎，固辭。

translations.literal: Su Gui's son Shen, styled Tingyan, placed at the top in the erudite and upright category, was appointed aide in Fenyin, promoted to detailed verification academician of the Secretariat, and repeatedly transferred to Supervising Secretary; at that time Ting was Vice Minister of the Palace Secretariat and firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: Su Gui's son Shen, whose style name was Tingyan, placed at the top in the erudite and upright examination, was appointed aide in Fenyin, promoted to detailed verification academician of the Secretariat, and eventually rose to Supervising Secretary. At that time Ting served as Vice Minister of the Palace Secretariat and firmly declined the appointment on his brother's behalf.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「古有內舉不避親者乎？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "In antiquity was there one who recommended from within and did not avoid kin?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Did not the ancients recommend kin from within without avoiding the appearance of favoritism?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「晉祁奚是也。」

translations.literal: He replied: "Qi Xi of Jin was such a one."
translations.idiomatic: He replied: "Qi Xi of Jin was such a man."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「若然，朕自用詵，卿言非公也。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "If so, I myself will use Shen—your words are not for the public good."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "If that is so, I shall appoint Shen myself. Your words are not disinterested."

sentences.zh: 頃之，出徐州刺史，治有跡。

translations.literal: Before long he was sent out as prefect of Xu Prefecture, and in governing there were visible achievements.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Shen was sent out as prefect of Xu Prefecture, where his governance left visible achievements.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously he was given Vice Minister of the Board of Civil Office.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously given the title Vice Minister of the Board of Civil Office.

sentences.zh: 詵子震，以蔭補千牛。

translations.literal: Shen's son Zhen, through yin privilege, was appointed Thousand-Ox Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Shen's son Zhen entered service through yin privilege as a Thousand-Ox Guard.

sentences.zh: 十餘歳，強學有成人風。

translations.literal: At more than ten years of age he studied strenuously and had the bearing of a mature man.
translations.idiomatic: By his teens he studied strenuously and showed the bearing of a mature man.

sentences.zh: 頲曰：「吾家有子。」

translations.literal: Ting said: "Our family has a son."
translations.idiomatic: Ting said: "Our family has produced a worthy son."

sentences.zh: 累遷殿中侍御史、長安令。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Attending Censor within the Palace and magistrate of Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the ranks to Attending Censor within the Palace and magistrate of Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 安祿山隱京師，震與尹崔光遠殺開遠門吏，棄家出奔。

translations.literal: When An Lushan concealed himself in the capital, Zhen with the magistrate Cui Guangyuan killed the gate officers of Kaiyuan Gate and abandoned his household to flee.
translations.idiomatic: When An Lushan was secretly in the capital, Zhen and the magistrate Cui Guangyuan killed the gate officers at Kaiyuan Gate and fled, abandoning their households.

sentences.zh: 會肅宗興師靈武，震晝夜馳及行在，帝嘉之，拜御史中丞，遷文部侍郎。

translations.literal: It happened that Emperor Suzong raised troops at Lingwu; Zhen rode day and night and reached the mobile court; the emperor praised him and appointed him Vice Censor-in-Chief, then promoted him to Vice Minister of the Board of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Suzong raised troops at Lingwu, Zhen rode day and night to reach the mobile court. The emperor praised him, appointed him Vice Censor-in-Chief, and later promoted him to Vice Minister of the Board of Rites.

sentences.zh: 廣平王爲元帥，崇擇賓佐，以震爲糧料使。

translations.literal: The Prince of Guangping was commander-in-chief; Chong selected staff and made Zhen grain commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Guangping served as commander-in-chief, Chong selected his staff and appointed Zhen grain commissioner.

sentences.zh: 二京平，封岐陽縣公，改河南尹。

translations.literal: When the two capitals were pacified, he was enfeoffed as Duke of Qiyang County and changed to Intendant of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: When the two capitals were recovered, he was enfeoffed as Duke of Qiyang County and appointed Intendant of Henan.

sentences.zh: 九節度兵敗相州，震與留守崔圓奔襄、鄧，貶濟王府長史。

translations.literal: When the armies of the nine military commissioners were defeated at Xiang Prefecture, Zhen with the garrison commander Cui Yuan fled to Xiang and Deng and was demoted to senior administrator of the Prince of Ji's household.
translations.idiomatic: When the armies of the nine military commissioners were defeated at Xiang Prefecture, Zhen fled with the garrison commander Cui Yuan to Xiang and Deng and was demoted to senior administrator of the Prince of Ji's household.

sentences.zh: 起爲絳州刺史，進戸部侍郎，判度支，爲泰陵、建陵鹵簿使，以勞封岐國公，拜太常卿。

translations.literal: He was recalled as prefect of Jiang Prefecture, advanced to Vice Minister of the Board of Revenue, given charge of the Treasury, made commissioner of honor guards for Tai and Jian mausoleums, enfeoffed as Duke of Qi for his labors, and appointed Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as prefect of Jiang Prefecture, promoted to Vice Minister of the Board of Revenue with charge of the Treasury, appointed commissioner of honor guards for the Tai and Jian mausoleums, enfeoffed as Duke of Qi for his labors, and appointed Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 代宗將幸東都，復以震爲河南尹，未行，卒，贈禮部尚書。

translations.literal: When Emperor Daizong was about to visit the eastern capital, Zhen was again made Intendant of Henan; before he could go he died and was posthumously given Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Daizong was about to visit the eastern capital, Zhen was again appointed Intendant of Henan. Before he could depart he died and was posthumously given the title Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 幹，瓌從父兄也。

translations.literal: Gan was Su Gui's cousin on the father's side.
translations.idiomatic: Gan was Su Gui's paternal cousin.

sentences.zh: 父勖，字慎行，武德中，爲秦王諮議、典簽、文學館學士，尚南康公主，拜駙馬都尉。

translations.literal: His father Xu, styled Shenxing, in the Wude era served as adviser to the Prince of Qin, keeper of records, and academician of the Hall for Cultivating Literature, married Princess Nankang, and was appointed Commandant of Escort.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xu, whose style name was Shenxing, served in the Wude era as adviser to the Prince of Qin, keeper of records, and academician of the Hall for Cultivating Literature. He married Princess Nankang and was appointed Commandant of Escort.

sentences.zh: 遷魏王泰府司馬，博學有美名，泰重之。

translations.literal: He was transferred to military aide of the Prince of Wei's household; erudite and with a fine reputation, Tai valued him.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to military aide in the household of Prince Tai of Wei. Learned and widely esteemed, Tai valued him highly.

sentences.zh: 勸開館引文學士，著書名家。

translations.literal: He urged opening a hall and drawing in literary scholars, and wrote books that made a name.
translations.idiomatic: He urged Tai to open a hall and gather literary scholars, and wrote books that won renown.

sentences.zh: 歷吏部侍郎、太子左庶子，卒。

translations.literal: He served as Vice Minister of the Board of Civil Office and Left Guardian of the Heir, and died.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Vice Minister of the Board of Civil Office and Left Guardian of the Heir Apparent, then died.

sentences.zh: 幹擢明經，授徐王府記室參軍，王好畋，每諫止之。

translations.literal: Gan was advanced through the mingjing examination and appointed recorder of the Prince of Xu's household; the prince loved hunting and he remonstrated and stopped him each time.
translations.idiomatic: Gan passed the mingjing examination and was appointed recorder in the household of the Prince of Xu. The prince loved hunting, and Gan remonstrated with him each time.

sentences.zh: 垂拱中，遷魏刺史。

translations.literal: In the Chuigong era he was transferred to prefect of Wei Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chuigong era he was transferred to prefect of Wei Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 河朔饑，前刺史苛暴，百姓流徙，幹檢吏督奸，勸課農桑，由是流冗盡復，以治稱。

translations.literal: The Hebei region was famine-stricken; the previous prefect was harsh and violent and the people fled; Gan inspected officials and supervised against corruption, urged agricultural and sericultural work, and thereby the displaced all returned—he was known for his governance.
translations.idiomatic: When famine struck the Hebei region, the previous prefect had been harsh and the people had fled. Gan inspected officials against corruption and urged agricultural work. The displaced population all returned, and he became known for his governance.

sentences.zh: 拜右羽林軍將軍，遷冬官尚書。

translations.literal: He was appointed General of the Right Forest Army and transferred to Minister of the Board of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed General of the Right Forest Army and promoted to Minister of the Board of Works.

sentences.zh: 來俊臣素忌之，誣幹與瑯邪王沖通書，繫獄，發憤卒。

translations.literal: Lai Junchen had long resented him and falsely accused Gan of exchanging letters with the Prince of Langye Chong; he was imprisoned and died in indignant rage.
translations.idiomatic: Lai Junchen had long resented him and falsely accused Gan of corresponding with the Prince of Langye, Chong. Gan was imprisoned and died of indignant rage.

sentences.zh: 張説張説，字道濟，或字説之，其先自范陽徙河南，更爲洛陽人。

translations.literal: Zhang Yue, styled Daoji or also styled Yuezhi—his ancestors moved from Fanyang to Henan and thereafter became men of Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yue, whose style name was Daoji or alternatively Yuezhi, came from a family that had moved from Fanyang to Henan and thereafter identified as natives of Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 永昌中，武后策賢良方正，詔吏部尚書李景諶糊名較覆，説所對第一，後署乙等，授太子校書郎，遷左補闕。

translations.literal: In the Yongchang era Empress Wu examined the erudite and upright; an edict had Vice Minister of the Board of Civil Office Li Jingchen compare with names concealed; Yue's answers ranked first, but later he was placed in the second grade and appointed collator of the Heir Apparent, then promoted to Left Remonstrator.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yongchang era Empress Wu examined candidates in the erudite and upright category. An edict had Li Jingchen of the Board of Civil Office compare answers with names concealed. Yue's answers ranked first, but he was ultimately placed in the second grade, appointed collator of the Heir Apparent, and later promoted to Left Remonstrator.

sentences.zh: 後嘗問：「諸儒言氏族皆本炎、黃之裔，則上古乃無百姓乎？

translations.literal: The empress once asked: "The various scholars say that clans and surnames all trace to descendants of Yan and Huang—then in high antiquity were there no common people?
translations.idiomatic: The empress once asked: "Scholars say that all clans trace their descent to Yan and Huang. Does that mean there were no common people in high antiquity?

sentences.zh: 若爲朕言之。」

translations.literal: Explain this for me."
translations.idiomatic: Explain this for me."

sentences.zh: 説曰：「古未有姓，若夷狄然。

translations.literal: Yue said: "In antiquity there were not yet surnames, as among the Yi and Di.
translations.idiomatic: Yue replied: "In antiquity there were not yet surnames, much as among the barbarians.

sentences.zh: 自炎帝之姜、黃帝之姬，始因所生地而爲之姓。

translations.literal: From the Jiang of Emperor Yan and the Ji of Emperor Huang, they first took as surnames the places where they were born.
translations.idiomatic: Beginning with the Jiang of Emperor Yan and the Ji of Emperor Huang, people first took as surnames the places where they were born.

sentences.zh: 其後天下建德，因生以賜姓，黃帝二十五子，而得姓者十四。

translations.literal: Afterward when the realm established virtue, surnames were bestowed according to birth; of the Yellow Emperor's twenty-five sons, fourteen received surnames.
translations.idiomatic: Later, as the realm established its moral order, surnames were bestowed according to birth. Of the Yellow Emperor's twenty-five sons, fourteen received surnames.

sentences.zh: 德同者姓同，德異者姓殊。

translations.literal: Those of the same virtue had the same surname; those of different virtue had different surnames.
translations.idiomatic: Those of the same virtue shared the same surname; those of different virtue received different surnames.

sentences.zh: 其後或以官，或以國，或以王父之字，始爲賜族，久乃爲姓。

translations.literal: Afterward some took office, some took state, some took the style character of the grandfather's father—as first bestowed clans, and only after long time did these become surnames.
translations.idiomatic: Later some took office titles, some took state names, and some took the style character of a grandfather's father as their clan designation. These were first bestowed as clans and only over time became surnames.

sentences.zh: 降唐、虞，抵戰國，姓族漸廣。

translations.literal: Descending from Tang and Yu down to the Warring States, surnames and clans gradually spread wide.
translations.idiomatic: From the eras of Tang and Yu down to the Warring States, surnames and clans gradually multiplied.

sentences.zh: 周衰，列國既滅，其民各以舊國爲之氏，下及兩漢，人皆有姓。

translations.literal: When Zhou declined and the feudal states were extinguished, their people each took their former states as their clan names; down to the two Han dynasties, everyone had a surname.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou declined and the feudal states were extinguished, their people each took their former states as clan names. By the two Han dynasties, everyone had a surname.

sentences.zh: 故姓之以國者，韓、陳、許、鄭、魯、衛、趙、魏爲多。」

translations.literal: Therefore among surnames taken from states, Han, Chen, Xu, Zheng, Lu, Wei, Zhao, and Wei were most numerous."
translations.idiomatic: Among surnames taken from states, Han, Chen, Xu, Zheng, Lu, Wei, Zhao, and Wei were the most numerous."

sentences.zh: 後曰：「善。」

translations.literal: The empress said: "Good."
translations.idiomatic: The empress said: "Well said."

sentences.zh: 久視中，後逭暑三陽宮，汔秋未還。

translations.literal: In the Jiushi era the empress escaped the heat at the Sanyang Palace and by nearly autumn had not returned.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jiushi era the empress retreated to the Sanyang Palace to escape the summer heat and had not returned even as autumn approached.

sentences.zh: 説上疏曰：

translations.literal: Yue submitted a memorial, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Yue submitted a memorial, saying:

sentences.zh: 宮距洛城百六十里，有伊水之隔，阪之峻，過夏涉秋，水潦方積，道壞山險，不通轉運，河廣無梁，咫尺千里，扈從兵馬，日費資餉。

translations.literal: The palace is one hundred sixty li from Luoyang, with the Yi River between and steep slopes; passing summer and entering autumn, floodwaters are accumulating, roads ruined and mountains dangerous, transport cannot pass, the river is wide without bridges—a thousand li within a foot's measure—the accompanying soldiers and horses daily consume provisions.
translations.idiomatic: The palace stands one hundred sixty li from Luoyang, separated by the Yi River and steep slopes. Summer has passed into autumn, floodwaters are rising, roads are ruined and mountains treacherous, and transport cannot get through. The river is wide and bridgeless—a thousand li within a foot's span. The accompanying soldiers and horses consume provisions daily.

sentences.zh: 太倉、武庫，並在都邑，紅粟、利器，蘊若山丘，奈何去宗朝之上都，安山谷之僻處？

translations.literal: The great granary and armory are both in the capital city; red grain and sharp weapons are stored like hills—how can we leave the supreme capital of the ancestral court and settle in a secluded valley?
translations.idiomatic: The great granary and armory are both in the capital. Red grain and sharp weapons are stored like hills. How can we leave the supreme capital of the ancestral court and settle in a secluded valley?

sentences.zh: 是猶倒持劍戟，示人樽柄，臣竊爲陛下不取。

translations.literal: This is like holding sword and halberd upside down and showing people the cup handle—your subject privately holds that Your Majesty should not take this course.
translations.idiomatic: This is like holding sword and halberd upside down and presenting the hilt to one's enemies. I hold that Your Majesty should not take this course.

sentences.zh: 夫禍變之生，在人所忽，故曰：「安樂必戒，無行所悔。」

translations.literal: Calamity and change arise from what people neglect; therefore it is said: "In ease and joy one must be vigilant—do not act what you will regret."
translations.idiomatic: Calamity arises from what people neglect. Therefore it is said: "In ease and joy one must remain vigilant—do not act in ways you will regret."

sentences.zh: 不可一也。

translations.literal: This is the first reason it cannot be done.
translations.idiomatic: That is my first objection.

sentences.zh: 宮城褊小，萬方輻湊，塡郛溢郭，並鍤無所。

translations.literal: The palace city is cramped and small; from the ten thousand directions people converge; they fill the outer walls and overflow the inner wards—there is nowhere even to drive a spade together.
translations.idiomatic: The palace city is cramped. People converge from every direction, filling the outer walls and overflowing the inner wards. There is nowhere even to stand shoulder to shoulder.

sentences.zh: 排斥居人，蓬宿草次，風雨暴至，不知庇托，孤惸老病，流轉衢巷。

translations.literal: Residents are driven out; they lodge in grass huts; when wind and rain strike suddenly they know not where to shelter; the orphaned, solitary, old, and sick wander through streets and lanes.
translations.idiomatic: Residents are driven out and lodge in grass huts. When storms strike suddenly they have no shelter. The orphaned, solitary, old, and sick wander through the streets.

sentences.zh: 陛下作人父母，將若之何？

translations.literal: Your Majesty is father and mother to the people—what will you do about this?
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty is father and mother to the people. What will you do about this?

sentences.zh: 不可二也。

translations.literal: This cannot be done—a second reason.
translations.idiomatic: That is my second objection.

sentences.zh: 池亭奇巧，蕩誘上心。

translations.literal: Pools and pavilions are marvelously ingenious and sway and entice the ruler's heart.
translations.idiomatic: Pools and pavilions of marvelous ingenuity sway and entice the ruler's heart.

sentences.zh: 削巒起觀，堨流漲海，俯貫地脈，仰出雲路，易山川之氣，奪農桑之土。

translations.literal: Mountains are cut down to raise towers; embankments divert streams and swell the sea; looking down they pierce the earth's pulse, looking up they rise into cloud paths; they alter the qi of mountains and rivers and seize the soil of farming and sericulture.
translations.idiomatic: Mountains are cut down to raise towers. Embankments divert streams and swell artificial lakes. Looking down they pierce the earth's pulse; looking up they rise into the clouds. They alter the spirit of mountains and rivers and seize land from farming and sericulture.

sentences.zh: 延木石，運斧斤，山谷連聲，春夏不輟。

translations.literal: Timber and stone are drawn in, axes and adzes are transported—the valleys echo with continuous sound, and in spring and summer there is no pause.
translations.idiomatic: Timber and stone are hauled in and axes never cease. The valleys echo with continuous sound, and work goes on without pause through spring and summer.

sentences.zh: 勸陛下作此者，豈正人邪？

translations.literal: Those who urge Your Majesty to do this—are they upright men?
translations.idiomatic: Those who urge Your Majesty to undertake this—are they upright men?

sentences.zh: 《詩》云：「人亦勞止，迄可小康。」

translations.literal: The Odes say: "The people also have labored long—surely they may have a little rest."
translations.idiomatic: The Odes say: "The people also have labored long—surely they may have a little rest."

sentences.zh: 不可三也。

translations.literal: This cannot be done—a third reason.
translations.idiomatic: That is my third objection.

sentences.zh: 禦苑東西二十里，外無墻垣扃禁，內有榛叢溪谷，猛毅所伏，暴慝所憑。

translations.literal: The imperial park extends twenty li east and west; outside there are no walls or barred gates; within are hazel thickets and stream valleys where fierce strength lies in wait and violent wickedness finds support.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial park extends twenty li east and west. It has no outer walls or barred gates, but within are thickets and stream valleys where fierce beasts lie in wait and violent men find refuge.

sentences.zh: 陛下往往輕行，警蹕不肅，歷蒙密，乘險巇，卒有逸獸狂夫，驚犯左右，豈不殆哉？

translations.literal: Your Majesty often travels lightly, with guards and halts not strict, passing through dense cover and riding dangerous slopes—if suddenly a runaway beast or madman should startle and violate those at your side, would it not be perilous?
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty often travels lightly, with guards not properly arrayed, passing through dense cover and riding dangerous slopes. If a runaway beast or madman should suddenly startle and strike those at your side, would that not be perilous?

sentences.zh: 《易》曰：「思患豫防。」

translations.literal: The Changes say: "Think of calamity and guard against it beforehand."
translations.idiomatic: The Changes say: "Think of calamity and guard against it beforehand."

sentences.zh: 願爲萬姓持重。

translations.literal: I wish to hold weight for the ten thousand surnames on Your Majesty's behalf.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that Your Majesty hold yourself in gravity for the sake of the people.

sentences.zh: 不可四也。

translations.literal: This cannot be done—a fourth reason.
translations.idiomatic: That is my fourth objection.

sentences.zh: 今北有胡寇覷邊，南有夷獠騷僥，關西小旱，耕稼是憂，安東近平，輸漕方始。

translations.literal: Now in the north Hu raiders watch the borders; in the south Yi and Liao stir restlessness; in Guanxi there is slight drought and farming is a worry; Andong is newly pacified and transport of grain has just begun.
translations.idiomatic: In the north barbarian raiders watch the borders. In the south tribal peoples stir unrest. Guanxi suffers slight drought and farming is at risk. Andong has only recently been pacified and grain transport has just begun.

sentences.zh: 臣願及時旋軫，深居上京，息人以展農，修德以來遠，罷不急之役，省無用之費。

translations.literal: Your subject wishes that Your Majesty turn the carriage wheel in time, dwell deeply in the upper capital, let the people rest to extend agriculture, cultivate virtue to draw the distant, halt non-urgent corvée, and reduce useless expenses.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that Your Majesty turn back in time, dwell securely in the upper capital, let the people rest so agriculture may flourish, cultivate virtue to draw the distant, halt non-urgent corvée, and reduce useless expenses.

sentences.zh: 澄心淡懷，惟億萬年，蒼蒼群生，莫不幸甚。

translations.literal: With clear heart and calm breast, for ten thousand myriad years—the vast multitude of living beings would all be most fortunate.
translations.idiomatic: With a clear heart and calm spirit, for ten thousand myriad years—the vast multitude of living beings would all be most fortunate.

sentences.zh: 臣度芻議，十不從一，何者？

translations.literal: Your subject estimates that of these rough counsels, not one in ten will be followed—why?
translations.idiomatic: I expect that of these rough counsels, not one in ten will be followed. Why?

sentences.zh: 沮盤遊之娛，間林沚之玩，規遠圖，替近適，要後利，棄前歡，未沃明主之心，已捩貴臣之意。

translations.literal: They obstruct the pleasure of roaming excursions, interrupt play in forest pools, plan distant designs, displace near comfort, seek later profit and abandon former delight—before the enlightened ruler's heart is watered, the honored ministers' intent is already twisted.
translations.idiomatic: They obstruct the pleasure of excursions, interrupt play in forest pools, plan for distant ends while displacing near comfort, seek later profit while abandoning present delight. Before the enlightened ruler's heart is won, the honored ministers' intent is already turned against me.

sentences.zh: 然不愛死者，懼言責不職耳。

translations.literal: Yet one who does not love death fears only that speech will bring the charge of failing in duty.
translations.idiomatic: Yet one who does not love death fears only that speech will bring the charge of failing in duty.

sentences.zh: 後不省。

translations.literal: The empress did not heed.
translations.idiomatic: The empress paid no heed.

sentences.zh: 擢鳳閣舍人。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Drafting Secretary of the Phoenix Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Drafting Secretary of the Phoenix Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 張易之誣陷魏元忠也，援説爲助。

translations.literal: When Zhang Yizhi falsely accused Wei Yuanzhong, he drew on Yue as helper.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Yizhi falsely accused Wei Yuanzhong, he enlisted Yue's support.

sentences.zh: 説廷對「元忠無不順言」，忤後旨，流欽州。

translations.literal: Yue answered in court that "Yuanzhong had no disloyal words," offending the empress's intent, and was banished to Qin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Yue answered in court that "Yuanzhong had spoken no disloyal words," offending the empress, and was banished to Qin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 中宗立，召爲兵部員外郎，累遷工部、兵部二侍郎，以母喪免。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhongzong took the throne, Yue was summoned as Supernumerary Vice Minister of the Board of War, repeatedly promoted to Vice Minister of the Boards of Works and War, and dismissed for his mother's mourning.
