translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhongzong took the throne, Yue was summoned as Supernumerary Vice Minister of the Board of War, successively promoted to Vice Minister of the Boards of Works and War, then dismissed for mourning his mother.

sentences.zh: 既期，詔起爲黃門侍郎，固請終制，祈陳哀到。

translations.literal: When the mourning period had ended, an edict recalled him as Vice Minister of the Palace Secretariat; he firmly asked to complete the full mourning term and prayed with grief expressed to the utmost.
translations.idiomatic: When the mourning period had ended, an edict recalled him as Vice Minister of the Palace Secretariat. He firmly asked to complete the full mourning term and pleaded with utmost grief.

sentences.zh: 時禮俗衰薄，士以奪服爲榮，而説獨以禮終，天下高之。

translations.literal: At that time ritual custom had declined and grown thin; gentlemen took cutting short mourning as glory, but Yue alone ended mourning according to ritual, and the realm honored him.
translations.idiomatic: At that time ritual custom had declined, and gentlemen took cutting short mourning as a mark of honor. Yue alone completed mourning according to ritual, and the realm honored him for it.

sentences.zh: 除喪，復爲兵部，兼修文館學士。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he returned to the Board of War and concurrently served as academician of the Hall for Cultivating Literature.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended he returned to the Board of War and concurrently served as academician of the Hall for Cultivating Literature.

sentences.zh: 睿宗即位，擢中書侍郎兼雍州長史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ruizong took the throne, he was advanced to Vice Minister of the Chancellery and concurrently senior administrator of Yong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ruizong took the throne, he was promoted to Vice Minister of the Chancellery and concurrently senior administrator of Yong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 譙王重福死，東都支黨數百人，獄久不決，詔説往按，一昔而罪人得，乃誅張靈均、鄭愔，餘詿誤悉原。

translations.literal: When Prince Chongfu of Qiao died, several hundred partisans in the eastern capital were long unresolved in prison; an edict sent Yue to investigate; in one night the guilty were obtained; Zhang Lingjun and Zheng Yin were executed and the rest who were misled were all pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Chongfu of Qiao died, several hundred partisans in the eastern capital languished unresolved in prison. An edict sent Yue to investigate. Within a single night the guilty were identified. Zhang Lingjun and Zheng Yin were executed, and the rest who had been misled were all pardoned.

sentences.zh: 帝嘉其不枉直，不漏惡，慰勞之。

translations.literal: The emperor praised him for not bending the upright and not letting evil slip through, and comforted and rewarded him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised him for not bending justice and not letting the guilty escape, and comforted and rewarded him.

sentences.zh: 玄宗爲太子，説與褚無量侍讀，尤見親禮。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuanzong was crown prince, Yue with Chu Wuliang served as lecturers in attendance and was especially shown intimate courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuanzong was crown prince, Yue and Chu Wuliang served as lecturers in attendance and were shown especial favor.

sentences.zh: 逾年，進同中書門下平章事，監修國史。

translations.literal: After a year he was advanced to Grand Counselor with the Chancellery and supervised editing of the national history.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he was promoted to Grand Counselor with the Chancellery and charged with supervising the national history.

sentences.zh: 景雲二年，帝謂侍臣曰：「術家言五日內有急兵入宮，爲我備之。」

translations.literal: In the second year of Jingyun the emperor told attending ministers: "The diviners say that within five days urgent troops will enter the palace—prepare for this on my behalf."
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jingyun the emperor told his attending ministers: "Diviners say that within five days urgent troops will enter the palace. Prepare for this."

sentences.zh: 左右莫對。

translations.literal: Those at his side had no reply.
translations.idiomatic: No one at his side had a reply.

sentences.zh: 説進曰：「此讒人謀動東宮耳，陛下若以太子監國，則名分定，奸膽破，蜚禍塞矣。」

translations.literal: Yue advanced and said: "This is slanderers plotting to stir the Eastern Palace. If Your Majesty has the crown prince supervise the state, then name and status are fixed, traitors' courage is broken, and flying calamity is blocked."
translations.idiomatic: Yue stepped forward and said: "This is slanderers plotting against the Eastern Palace. If Your Majesty has the crown prince supervise the state, name and status will be fixed, traitors' courage broken, and flying calamity blocked."

sentences.zh: 帝悟，下制如説言。

translations.literal: The emperor understood and issued an edict as Yue had said.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor understood and issued an edict as Yue had advised.

sentences.zh: 明年，皇太子即皇帝位，太平公主引蕭至忠、崔湜等爲宰相，以説不附己，授尚書左丞，罷政事，爲東都留守。

translations.literal: The next year the crown prince took the imperial throne; Princess Taiping brought in Xiao Zhizhong, Cui Shi, and others as chief ministers; because Yue did not attach to her, he was given Left Vice Director of the Board of Works, removed from government affairs, and made garrison commander of the eastern capital.
translations.idiomatic: The next year the crown prince took the throne. Princess Taiping installed Xiao Zhizhong, Cui Shi, and others as chief ministers. Because Yue would not attach himself to her faction, he was appointed Left Vice Director of the Board of Works, removed from government affairs, and made garrison commander of the eastern capital.

sentences.zh: 説知太平等懷逆，乃因使以佩刀獻玄宗，請先決策，帝納之。

translations.literal: Yue knew that Taiping and her faction harbored treason; he therefore through an envoy presented his girdle knife to Emperor Xuanzong and asked him to decide first; the emperor accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: Yue knew that Princess Taiping and her faction harbored treason. Through an envoy he presented his girdle knife to Emperor Xuanzong and urged him to act first. The emperor accepted it.

sentences.zh: 至忠等已誅，召爲中書令，封燕國公，實封二百戸。

translations.literal: When Zhizhong and the others had been executed, he was summoned as Chief Minister of the Chancellery, enfeoffed as Duke of Yan, with a substantive fief of two hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhizhong and the others were executed, he was summoned as Chief Minister of the Chancellery, enfeoffed as Duke of Yan, with a substantive fief of two hundred households.

sentences.zh: 始，武后末年，爲潑寒胡戲，中宗嘗乘樓從觀。

translations.literal: At the beginning, in the last years of Empress Wu, there was the po-han-hu play; Emperor Zhongzong once mounted a tower to watch it.
translations.idiomatic: In the last years of Empress Wu there was the po-han-hu play, and Emperor Zhongzong once mounted a tower to watch it.

sentences.zh: 至是，因四夷來朝，復爲之。

translations.literal: At this time, because the four barbarians came to court, it was performed again.
translations.idiomatic: Now, because the four barbarians had come to court, the performance was revived.

sentences.zh: 説上疏曰：「韓宣適魯，見周禮而嘆，孔子會齊，數倡優之罪。

translations.literal: Yue submitted a memorial, saying: "Han Xuan went to Lu and sighed upon seeing the Zhou rituals; Confucius met with Qi and repeatedly counted the crimes of performers and jesters.
translations.idiomatic: Yue submitted a memorial: "When Han Xuan went to Lu he sighed upon seeing the Zhou rituals. When Confucius met with Qi he repeatedly condemned the crimes of performers and jesters.

sentences.zh: 列國如此，況天朝乎？

translations.literal: The feudal states were thus—how much more the celestial court?
translations.idiomatic: If the feudal states were thus, how much more the celestial court?

sentences.zh: 今四夷請和，使者入謁，當按以禮樂，示以兵威，雖曰戎夷，不可輕也。

translations.literal: Now the four barbarians seek peace and envoys enter to pay homage—they should be received according to ritual and music and shown military might; though called Rong and Yi, they cannot be treated lightly.
translations.idiomatic: Now the four barbarians seek peace and envoys come to pay homage. They should be received with ritual and music and shown military might. Though called barbarians, they cannot be treated lightly.

sentences.zh: 焉知無駒支之辯，由餘之賢哉？

translations.literal: How do we know there is not a Ju Zhi in eloquence or a You Yu in worth?
translations.idiomatic: How do we know there is not among them another Ju Zhi in eloquence or You Yu in talent?

sentences.zh: 且乞寒潑胡，未聞典故，裸體跳足，汨泥揮水，盛德何觀焉？

translations.literal: Moreover the qi-han po-hu is not heard of in classical precedent—naked bodies, leaping feet, splashing mud and flinging water—what great virtue is there to behold?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the qi-han po-hu is unheard of in classical precedent. Naked bodies, leaping feet, splashing mud and flinging water—what great virtue is there to behold in this?

sentences.zh: 恐非幹羽柔遠，樽俎折沖之道。」

translations.literal: I fear this is not the way of shield and feather to soften the distant, or of goblet and platter to break the enemy's charge."
translations.idiomatic: I fear this is not the way of civil virtue to soften the distant, or of diplomacy to break the enemy's charge."

sentences.zh: 納之，自是遂絶。

translations.literal: The emperor accepted it, and from this time the practice was ended.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted his advice, and from that time the practice was ended.

sentences.zh: 素與姚元崇不平，罷爲相州刺史、河北道按察使。

translations.literal: He had long been on bad terms with Yao Chong; he was dismissed as prefect of Xiang Prefecture and inspector of the Hebei circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He had long been at odds with Yao Chong and was dismissed to serve as prefect of Xiang Prefecture and inspector of the Hebei circuit.

sentences.zh: 坐累徙岳州，停實封。

translations.literal: Through accumulated offenses he was transferred to Yue Prefecture and his substantive fief was suspended.
translations.idiomatic: Through accumulated offenses he was transferred to Yue Prefecture and his substantive fief was suspended.

sentences.zh: 説既失執政意，內自懼。

translations.literal: Yue, having lost the intent to hold power, was inwardly afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Having lost power, Yue was inwardly afraid.

sentences.zh: 雅與蘇瓌善，時瓌子頲爲宰相，因作《五君詠》獻頲，其一紀瓌也，候瓌忌日致之。

translations.literal: He had long been on good terms with Su Gui; at that time Gui's son Ting was chief minister; he therefore composed the "Odes to Five Gentlemen" and presented them to Ting, one of which commemorated Gui, and on Gui's death anniversary sent it.
translations.idiomatic: He had long been friendly with Su Gui. At that time Gui's son Ting served as chief minister. Yue composed the "Odes to Five Gentlemen" and presented them to Ting, one commemorating Gui, which he sent on Gui's death anniversary.

sentences.zh: 頲覽詩嗚咽，未幾，見帝陳説忠謇有勛，不宜棄外，遂遷荊州長史。

translations.literal: Ting read the poems and wept; before long he saw the emperor and stated that Yue was loyal and upright with merit and should not be cast outward; he was therefore transferred to senior administrator of Jing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Ting read the poems and wept. Before long he told the emperor that Yue was loyal and upright and had rendered merit, and should not be cast aside. Yue was therefore transferred to senior administrator of Jing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 俄以右羽林將軍檢校幽州都督，入朝以戎服見。

translations.literal: Before long, as General of the Right Forest Army with acting commission as metropolitan governor of You, he entered court and was received in military dress.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, as General of the Right Forest Army with acting commission as metropolitan governor of You, he entered court in military dress.

sentences.zh: 帝大喜，授檢校并州長史，兼天兵軍大使，修國史，敕賫稿即軍中論撰。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased and appointed him acting senior administrator of Bing Prefecture and concurrently commissioner of the Heavenly Troops Army, editing the national history, with an edict delivering drafts so he could compose and discuss them in the army.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was greatly pleased and appointed him acting senior administrator of Bing Prefecture and concurrently commissioner of the Heavenly Troops Army, with charge of editing the national history. An edict delivered drafts so he could compose and discuss them in camp.

sentences.zh: 朔方軍大使王晙誅河曲降虜阿布思也，九姓同羅、拔野固等皆疑懼。

translations.literal: Wang Jun, commissioner of the Shuofang Army, executed the surrendered captive Abu Si of the river bend; the nine surnames Tongluo, Bayegu, and others were all suspicious and fearful.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun, commissioner of the Shuofang Army, executed the surrendered captive Abu Si of the river bend. The nine surnames Tongluo, Bayegu, and others were all suspicious and fearful.

sentences.zh: 説持節從輕騎二十，直詣其部，宿帳下，召見酋豪慰安之。

translations.literal: Yue held credentials and with twenty light horsemen went straight to their encampment, lodged beneath their tents, summoned and saw the chieftains and nobles, and comforted them.
translations.idiomatic: Yue took credentials and with twenty light horsemen rode straight to their encampment. He lodged beneath their tents, summoned the chieftains, and comforted them.

sentences.zh: 副使李憲以虜難信，不宜涉不測。

translations.literal: Vice commissioner Li Xian held that the barbarians were hard to trust and one should not venture into the unpredictable.
translations.idiomatic: Vice commissioner Li Xian argued that the barbarians were untrustworthy and one should not venture into the unpredictable.

sentences.zh: 説報曰：「吾肉非黃羊，不畏其食；

translations.literal: Yue replied: "My flesh is not yellow sheep—they need not fear to eat it;
translations.idiomatic: Yue replied: "My flesh is not that of yellow sheep—they need not fear to eat it.

sentences.zh: 血非野馬，不畏其刺。

translations.literal: my blood is not wild horse—they need not fear to pierce it.
translations.idiomatic: My blood is not that of wild horse—they need not fear to pierce it.

sentences.zh: 士當見危致命，亦吾效死秋也。」

translations.literal: A gentleman should meet danger and give his life—this too is my season to die in effect."
translations.idiomatic: A gentleman should meet danger and give his life. This too is my season to die in duty."

sentences.zh: 由是九姓遂安。

translations.literal: Thereby the nine surnames were settled in peace.
translations.idiomatic: Thereby the nine surnames were settled in peace.

sentences.zh: 晙後討蘭池叛胡康待賓，詔説相聞經略。

translations.literal: Later Jun campaigned against the rebel Hu Kang Daibin of Lanchi Pool; an edict had Yue coordinate strategy by communication.
translations.idiomatic: Later Jun campaigned against the rebel Hu Kang Daibin of Lanchi Pool. An edict had Yue coordinate strategy with him.

sentences.zh: 時党項羌亦連兵攻銀城，説將歩騎萬人出合河關掩擊，破之，追北駱駝堰。

translations.literal: At that time the Tangut Qiang also linked arms to attack Yincheng; Yue led ten thousand infantry and cavalry out through Hehe Pass in a surprise attack, defeated them, and pursued north to Luotuo Weir.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Tangut Qiang also joined forces to attack Yincheng. Yue led ten thousand infantry and cavalry out through Hehe Pass in a surprise attack, defeated them, and pursued north to Luotuo Weir.

sentences.zh: 羌、胡自相猜，夜鬥，待賓遁入鐵建山，餘眾奔潰。

translations.literal: The Qiang and Hu suspected one another and fought at night; Daibin fled into Mount Tiejian and the rest of the host scattered in rout.
translations.idiomatic: The Qiang and Hu suspected one another and fought at night. Daibin fled into Mount Tiejian and the rest scattered in rout.

sentences.zh: 説招納党項，使復故處。

translations.literal: Yue recruited and accepted the Tangut and had them return to their former places.
translations.idiomatic: Yue recruited the Tangut and had them return to their former places.

sentences.zh: 副使史獻請盡誅之，説不從，奏置麟州以安羌眾。

translations.literal: Vice commissioner Shi Xian asked to execute them all; Yue did not follow this and memorialized to establish Lin Prefecture to settle the Qiang multitude.
translations.idiomatic: Vice commissioner Shi Xian asked to execute them all. Yue refused and memorialized to establish Lin Prefecture to settle the Qiang population.

sentences.zh: 召拜兵部尚書、同中書門下三品，讓宋璟、陸象先，不許。

translations.literal: He was summoned and appointed Minister of War and Grand Counselor with the Chancellery; he yielded to Song Jing and Lu Xiangxian, but this was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned and appointed Minister of War and Grand Counselor with the Chancellery. He yielded precedence to Song Jing and Lu Xiangxian, but the emperor would not permit it.

sentences.zh: 明年，詔爲朔方節度大使，親行五城，督士馬。

translations.literal: The next year an edict made him military commissioner of Shuofang; he personally toured the five cities and supervised soldiers and horses.
translations.idiomatic: The next year an edict made him military commissioner of Shuofang. He personally toured the five cities and supervised troops and horses.

sentences.zh: 時慶州方渠降胡康願子反，自爲可汗，掠牧馬，西涉河出塞。

translations.literal: At that time the surrendered Hu Kang Yuanzi of Fangqu in Qing Prefecture rebelled, made himself khan, plundered pasture horses, and west of the river crossed out of the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the surrendered Hu Kang Yuanzi of Fangqu in Qing Prefecture rebelled, declared himself khan, plundered pasture horses, and crossed west of the river out of the frontier.

sentences.zh: 説進討，至木槃山禽之，俘獲三千。

translations.literal: Yue advanced to campaign, reached Mount Mupan and captured him, taking three thousand captives.
translations.idiomatic: Yue advanced against him, captured him at Mount Mupan, and took three thousand captives.

sentences.zh: 乃議徙河曲六州殘胡五萬於唐、鄧仙、豫間，空河南朔方地。

translations.literal: He then proposed moving fifty thousand remnant Hu of the six prefectures of the river bend to among Tang, Deng, Xian, and Yu, emptying the Henan and Shuofang lands.
translations.idiomatic: He then proposed moving fifty thousand remnant Hu of the six river-bend prefectures to the regions of Tang, Deng, Xian, and Yu, emptying the Henan and Shuofang frontier lands.

sentences.zh: 以功賜實封三百戸。

translations.literal: For his merit he was granted a substantive fief of three hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit he was granted a substantive fief of three hundred households.

sentences.zh: 故時，邊鎮兵嬴六十萬，説以時平無所事，請罷二十萬還農。

translations.literal: In former times border garrison troops numbered six hundred thousand; Yue held that in this peaceful age there was nothing for them to do and asked to dismiss two hundred thousand back to farming.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly border garrison troops numbered six hundred thousand. Yue held that in this peaceful age they had little to do and asked to dismiss two hundred thousand back to farming.

sentences.zh: 天子以爲疑，説曰：「邊兵雖廣，諸將自衛、營私爾，所以制敵，不在眾也。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven was doubtful; Yue said: "Though border troops are many, the generals only defend themselves and pursue private gain—in controlling the enemy, numbers are not what matter.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was doubtful. Yue said: "Though border troops are numerous, the generals only defend themselves and pursue private gain. In controlling the enemy, numbers are not what matter.

sentences.zh: 以陛下之明，四夷畏威，不慮減兵而招寇，臣請以闔門百口爲保。」

translations.literal: With Your Majesty's enlightenment, the four barbarians fear your might—I do not worry that reducing troops will invite raiders; your subject asks to guarantee this with the hundred mouths of his entire household."
translations.idiomatic: With Your Majesty's enlightenment, the four barbarians fear your might. I do not fear that reducing troops will invite raiders. I ask to guarantee this with the lives of my entire household."

sentences.zh: 帝乃可。

translations.literal: The emperor then approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 時衛兵貧弱，番休者亡命略盡，説建請一切募勇強士，優其科條，簡色役。

translations.literal: At that time palace guards were poor and weak; those on rotation for rest had nearly all fled as outlaws; Yue proposed recruiting all brave and strong men, favoring their regulations, and simplifying corvée labor.
translations.idiomatic: At that time palace guards were poor and weak, and those on rotation had nearly all fled. Yue proposed recruiting brave and strong men, offering favorable terms and simplifying corvée obligations.

sentences.zh: 不旬日，得勝兵十三萬，分補諸衛，以強京師，後所謂「廣騎」者也。

translations.literal: Within ten days he obtained one hundred thirty thousand victorious troops, distributed them to supplement the various guards, and thereby strengthened the capital—this was what was later called the "Expanded Cavalry."
translations.idiomatic: Within ten days he obtained one hundred thirty thousand elite troops, distributed them among the various guards to strengthen the capital. This was what was later called the "Expanded Cavalry."

sentences.zh: 帝自東都將還京，因幸并州。

translations.literal: The emperor, about to return from the eastern capital to the capital, took the occasion to visit Bing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: As the emperor was about to return from the eastern capital to Chang'an, he took the occasion to visit Bing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 説見帝曰：「太原王業所基，陛下巡幸，振耀威武，以申永思。

translations.literal: Yue saw the emperor and said: "Taiyuan is where the royal enterprise was founded; Your Majesty's tour displays martial might and extends eternal remembrance.
translations.idiomatic: Yue told the emperor: "Taiyuan is where the royal enterprise was founded. Your Majesty's tour displays martial might and extends eternal remembrance.

sentences.zh: 繇河東入京師，有漢武脽上祠，此禮廢闊，歷代莫舉，願爲三農祈穀，誠四海之福。」

translations.literal: Coming from Hedong into the capital, there is the shrine on the mound of Emperor Wu of Han—this ritual has been abandoned and neglected, and no dynasty has performed it; I wish to pray for the three crops and grain harvest—it would truly be fortune for the four seas."
translations.idiomatic: Coming from Hedong into the capital, there is the shrine on the mound of Emperor Wu of Han. This ritual has long been abandoned, and no dynasty has performed it. I ask that Your Majesty pray for the three crops and the harvest—it would truly be fortune for the four seas."

sentences.zh: 帝納其言，過祠后土乃還。

translations.literal: The emperor accepted his words, passed the shrine to worship the Queen of Earth, and then returned.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted his advice, worshipped at the shrine to the Queen of Earth, and then returned.

sentences.zh: 進中書令。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Chief Minister of the Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Chief Minister of the Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 説又倡封禪議，受詔與諸儒草儀，多所裁正。

translations.literal: Yue also advocated the fengshan proposal, received an edict to draft the ritual together with various scholars, and corrected much.
translations.idiomatic: Yue also advocated the fengshan proposal, received an edict to draft the ritual with various scholars, and corrected much of their work.

sentences.zh: 帝召説與禮官學士置酒集仙殿，曰：「朕今與賢者樂於此，當遂爲集賢殿。」

translations.literal: The emperor summoned Yue and ritual officials and academicians to set out wine in the Hall of Collected Immortals, saying: "I now take joy here with the worthy—this should forthwith become the Hall of Collected Worthies."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned Yue and ritual officials and academicians to feast in the Hall of Collected Immortals. He said: "I now take joy here with the worthy. This hall should forthwith become the Hall of Collected Worthies."

sentences.zh: 乃下制改麗正書院爲集賢殿書院，而授説院學士，知院事。

translations.literal: He then issued an edict changing the Lizheng Academy into the Collected Worthies Hall Academy and appointed Yue academy academician in charge of academy affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He then issued an edict changing the Lizheng Academy into the Collected Worthies Hall Academy and appointed Yue academician in charge of its affairs.

sentences.zh: 東封還，爲尚書右丞相兼中書令。

translations.literal: On return from the eastern fengshan he became Right Chief Minister of the Board of Works and concurrently Chief Minister of the Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: On return from the eastern fengshan he became Right Chief Minister of the Board of Works and concurrently Chief Minister of the Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 詔説撰《封禪壇頌》，刻之泰山，以誇成功。

translations.literal: An edict commanded Yue to compose the "Ode to the Fengshan Altar," carve it on Mount Tai, and thereby boast of successful achievement.
translations.idiomatic: An edict commanded Yue to compose the "Ode to the Fengshan Altar" and carve it on Mount Tai to commemorate the achievement.

sentences.zh: 初，源乾曜不欲封禪，説固請，乃不相平。

translations.literal: At the beginning Yuan Qianyao did not wish for the fengshan; Yue firmly requested it—they were therefore not on good terms.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning Yuan Qianyao opposed the fengshan, while Yue firmly advocated it. They were therefore not on good terms.

sentences.zh: 及升山，執事官當從者，説皆引所厚超階入五品，從兵唯加勛而不賜，眾怨其專。

translations.literal: When ascending the mountain, for attending officials who should follow, Yue all drew those he favored to leap ranks into the fifth grade; accompanying soldiers received only merit additions without gifts—the multitude resented his monopoly.
translations.idiomatic: When ascending the mountain, Yue advanced all his favorites among the attending officials by leap ranks into the fifth grade. Accompanying soldiers received only merit additions without gifts. Many resented his monopoly of favor.

sentences.zh: 宇文融先獻策，括天下遊戸及籍外田，署十道勸農使，分行郡縣。

translations.literal: Yuwen Rong first presented a plan to tally wandering households throughout the realm and fields outside the registers, appointing ten-circuit commissioners to encourage agriculture who traveled through prefectures and counties.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Rong first presented a plan to tally wandering households and fields outside the registers throughout the realm, appointing ten-circuit commissioners to encourage agriculture who traveled through prefectures and counties.

sentences.zh: 説畏其擾，數沮格之。

translations.literal: Yue feared the disturbance and repeatedly obstructed and blocked it.
translations.idiomatic: Yue feared the disturbance and repeatedly obstructed the plan.

sentences.zh: 至是，融請吏部置十銓，與蘇釐等分治選事，有所論請，説頗抑之，於是銓綜失敘。

translations.literal: At this time Rong asked the Board of Civil Office to establish ten selection boards, and with Su Li and others to divide governance of appointment affairs; when there were petitions and requests, Yue considerably suppressed them, and thereby the overall selection order was lost.
translations.idiomatic: At this time Rong asked the Board of Civil Office to establish ten selection boards, which he and Su Li and others would divide among themselves. When petitions arose, Yue considerably suppressed them, and the overall selection order was lost.

sentences.zh: 融恨恚，乃與崔隱甫、李林甫共劾奏説「引術士王慶則夜祠禱解，而奏表其閭；

translations.literal: Rong hated and resented this; he therefore with Cui Yinpu and Li Linfu jointly memorialized accusing Yue: "He drew in the technician Wang Qingze to perform night sacrifices and prayers for release, yet memorialized praising his neighborhood;
translations.idiomatic: Rong hated this and joined with Cui Yinpu and Li Linfu in a joint memorial accusing Yue: "He drew in the technician Wang Qingze to perform night sacrifices and prayers for release, yet memorialized praising his neighborhood.

sentences.zh: 引僧道岸窺诇時事，冒署右職；

translations.literal: he drew in the monk Dao'an to spy on current affairs and presumptuously appointed him to a high post;
translations.idiomatic: He drew in the monk Dao'an to spy on current affairs and presumptuously appointed him to a high post.

sentences.zh: 所親吏張觀、範堯臣依據説勢，市權招賂，擅給太原九姓羊錢千萬。」

translations.literal: his favored clerks Zhang Guan and Fan Yaochan relied on Yue's power, traded authority and solicited bribes, and on their own authority gave the nine surnames of Taiyuan sheep money in the tens of millions."
translations.idiomatic: His favored clerks Zhang Guan and Fan Yaochan relied on Yue's power, traded authority for bribes, and on their own authority gave the nine surnames of Taiyuan sheep money in the tens of millions."

sentences.zh: 其言醜慘。

translations.literal: Their words were ugly and dire.
translations.idiomatic: Their accusations were ugly and dire.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，詔乾曜、隱甫、刑部尚書韋抗即尚書省鞫之，發金吾兵圍其第。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry; an edict had Qianyao, Yinpu, and Vice Minister of Punishments Wei Kang immediately interrogate at the Board of Works and dispatched Golden Crow troops to surround his residence.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious. An edict had Qianyao, Yinpu, and Vice Minister of Punishments Wei Kang interrogate the case immediately at the Board of Works and dispatched Golden Crow troops to surround Yue's residence.

sentences.zh: 説兄左庶子光詣朝堂刑耳列冤，帝遣高力士往視，見説蓬首垢面，席槁，家人以瓦器饋脫粟鹽疏，爲自罰憂懼者。

translations.literal: Yue's elder brother, Left Guardian of the Heir Guang, went to the court hall and cut his ear to display injustice; the emperor sent Gao Lishi to look; he saw Yue with disheveled hair and filthy face, sitting on straw, his family feeding him husked grain and salt vegetables in earthenware vessels, as one punishing himself in worry and fear.
translations.idiomatic: Yue's elder brother Guang, Left Guardian of the Heir Apparent, went to the court hall and cut his ear to proclaim injustice. The emperor sent Gao Lishi to look. He found Yue with disheveled hair and filthy face, sitting on straw, his family feeding him coarse grain and salt vegetables in earthenware vessels, as one punishing himself in fear.

sentences.zh: 力士還奏，且言：「説往納忠，於國有功。」

translations.literal: Lishi returned and reported, also saying: "Yue in the past offered loyalty and had merit for the state."
translations.idiomatic: Lishi returned and reported, adding: "Yue in the past offered loyal counsel and rendered merit to the state."

sentences.zh: 帝憮然，乃停説中書令，誅慶則等，坐者猶十餘人。

translations.literal: The emperor was dismayed and therefore suspended Yue as Chief Minister of the Chancellery, executed Qingze and others, and those implicated still numbered more than ten.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was moved and suspended Yue as Chief Minister of the Chancellery, executed Qingze and others, and more than ten others were implicated.

sentences.zh: 説既罷政事，在集賢院專脩國史。

translations.literal: Yue, having been removed from government affairs, in the Collected Worthies Academy devoted himself solely to editing the national history.
translations.idiomatic: Having been removed from government affairs, Yue devoted himself solely to editing the national history in the Collected Worthies Academy.

sentences.zh: 又乞停右丞相，不許。

translations.literal: He again asked to suspend his post as Right Chief Minister; this was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: He again asked to resign as Right Chief Minister, but the request was denied.

sentences.zh: 然每軍國大務，帝輒訪焉。

translations.literal: Yet whenever there were great affairs of army and state, the emperor would consult him.
translations.idiomatic: Yet whenever great affairs of army and state arose, the emperor still consulted him.

sentences.zh: 隱甫等恐説復用，巧文詆毀，素忿説者又著《疾邪篇》，帝聞，因令致仕。

translations.literal: Yinpu and the others feared Yue would be reused and with clever words slandered and destroyed him; those who had long resented Yue also wrote the "Chapter on Hating Evil"; the emperor heard of it and therefore ordered him to retire.
translations.idiomatic: Yinpu and the others feared Yue would be restored to power and slandered him with clever words. Those who had long resented Yue also wrote the "Chapter on Hating Evil." When the emperor heard of this, he ordered Yue to retire.

sentences.zh: 始爲相時，帝欲事吐蕃，説密請講和以休息鄣塞，帝曰：「朕待王君㚟計之。」

translations.literal: When he first became chief minister, the emperor wished to campaign against Tibet; Yue secretly asked to negotiate peace to give rest to the frontier passes; the emperor said: "I await Wang Jun's plan for this."
translations.idiomatic: When he first became chief minister, the emperor wished to campaign against Tibet. Yue secretly asked to negotiate peace to give the frontier passes rest. The emperor said: "I await Wang Jun's plan for this."

sentences.zh: 説出告源乾曜曰：「君㚟好兵以求利，彼入，吾言不用矣。」

translations.literal: Yue went out and told Yuan Qianyao: "Jun loves warfare to seek profit—when he enters, my words will not be used."
translations.idiomatic: Yue went out and told Yuan Qianyao: "Jun loves warfare to seek profit. Once he is involved, my counsel will not be heeded."

sentences.zh: 後君㚟破吐蕃於青海西，説策其且敗，因上巂州鬥羊於帝，以申諷諭，曰：「使羊能言，必將曰『鬥而不解，立有死者』。

translations.literal: Later Jun defeated Tibet west of Qinghai; Yue calculated that he would soon be defeated and therefore presented to the emperor the Xi Prefecture ram-fighting sport as indirect admonition, saying: "If sheep could speak, they would surely say, 'We fight but do not understand—standing there are those who must die.'
translations.idiomatic: Later Jun defeated Tibet west of Qinghai. Yue calculated that Jun would soon fail and presented the Xi Prefecture ram-fighting sport to the emperor as indirect admonition, saying: "If sheep could speak, they would surely say, 'We fight without understanding—and standing there are those who must die.'

sentences.zh: 所賴至仁無殘，量力取歡焉。」

translations.literal: What is relied upon is utmost benevolence without cruelty—measuring strength and taking joy accordingly."
translations.idiomatic: What is relied upon is utmost benevolence without cruelty—measuring one's strength and taking joy accordingly."

sentences.zh: 帝識其意，納之，賜彩千匹。

translations.literal: The emperor understood his intent, accepted it, and granted a thousand bolts of colored silk.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor understood his intent, accepted the admonition, and granted a thousand bolts of colored silk.

sentences.zh: 後瓜州失守，君㚟死。

translations.literal: Later Guazhou was lost and Jun died.
translations.idiomatic: Later Guazhou fell and Jun died.

sentences.zh: 十七年，復爲右丞相，遷左丞相。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he was again made Right Chief Minister and transferred to Left Chief Minister.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he was again appointed Right Chief Minister and then transferred to Left Chief Minister.

sentences.zh: 上日，敕所司供帳設樂，內出醪饌，帝爲賦詩。

translations.literal: On the day he took office, an edict commanded the relevant offices to supply tents and set out music; wine and food were brought from within the palace, and the emperor composed a poem for him.
translations.idiomatic: On the day he took office, an edict commanded the relevant offices to supply tents and set out music. Wine and food were brought from within the palace, and the emperor composed a poem in his honor.

sentences.zh: 俄授開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: Before long he was granted Grand Master with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon of the First Rank.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was granted the title Grand Master with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon of the First Rank.

sentences.zh: 十八年卒，年六十四，爲停正會，贈太師，謚曰文貞，群臣駁異未決，帝爲制碑，謚如太常，繇是定。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he died at age sixty-four; regular court sessions were suspended; posthumously he was given Grand Preceptor and the posthumous title Wenzhen; the ministers disputed and had not decided; the emperor composed the stele inscription; the posthumous title followed the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and thereby it was settled.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year he died at the age of sixty-four. Regular court sessions were suspended. Posthumously he was given Grand Preceptor with the posthumous name Wenzhen. When ministers disputed the title, the emperor composed the stele inscription himself. The Court of Imperial Sacrifices' recommendation was followed, and the matter was settled.

sentences.zh: 説敦氣節，立然諾，喜推藉後進，於君臣朋友大義甚篤。

translations.literal: Yue was earnest in integrity and spirit, established his word as bond, delighted in promoting and supporting juniors, and in the great righteousness between ruler and minister and among friends was very devoted.
translations.idiomatic: Yue was earnest in integrity, kept his word as bond, delighted in promoting younger men, and was deeply devoted to the great obligations between ruler and minister and among friends.

sentences.zh: 帝在東宮，所與秘謀密計甚眾，後卒爲宗臣。

translations.literal: When the emperor was in the Eastern Palace, the secret plots and confidential plans shared with him were very numerous; he later ended as a pillar minister of the state.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor was crown prince, Yue shared many secret plots and confidential plans with him. He later became a pillar minister of the state.

sentences.zh: 朝廷大述作多出其手，帝好文辭，有所爲必使視草。

translations.literal: Great compositions of the court mostly came from his hand; the emperor loved literary expression and whenever he had something to compose would have Yue review the draft.
translations.idiomatic: Great state compositions mostly came from his hand. The emperor loved literary expression and whenever he composed something would have Yue review the draft.

sentences.zh: 善用人之長，多引天下知名士，以佐佑王化，粉澤典章，成一王法。

translations.literal: He was skilled in using men's strengths, drew in many renowned gentlemen of the realm to assist and support royal transformation, adorned canonical regulations, and completed the law of a true king.
translations.idiomatic: He was skilled in using men's strengths, drew in many renowned gentlemen of the realm to assist royal governance, adorned canonical regulations, and helped complete the law of a true king.

sentences.zh: 天子尊尚經術，開館置學士，脩太宗之政，皆説倡之。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven honored and upheld classical learning, opened halls and appointed academicians, and restored the governance of Emperor Taizong—all were advocated by Yue.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor honored classical learning, opened halls and appointed academicians, and restored the governance of Emperor Taizong—all were advocated by Yue.

sentences.zh: 爲文屬思精壯，長於碑誌，世所不逮。

translations.literal: In writing he focused thought with refined vigor and excelled at steles and records—what the age could not match.
translations.idiomatic: In writing he focused his thought with refined vigor and excelled at steles and memorial inscriptions—skills the age could not match.

sentences.zh: 既謫岳州，而詩益淒婉，人謂得江山助雲。

translations.literal: After he was banished to Yue Prefecture, his poetry grew more plaintive and gentle; people said he obtained the help of rivers and mountains.
translations.idiomatic: After he was banished to Yue Prefecture, his poetry grew more plaintive and gentle. People said he had obtained the help of rivers and mountains.

sentences.zh: 常典集賢圖書之任，間雖致仕一歳，亦修史於家。

translations.literal: He constantly held charge of the books of the Collected Worthies Academy; even when he retired for a year in between, he still edited history at home.
translations.idiomatic: He constantly held charge of the books of the Collected Worthies Academy. Even when he retired for a year in between, he still edited history at home.

sentences.zh: 始，帝欲授説大學士，辭曰：「學士本無大稱，中宗崇寵大臣，乃有之，臣不敢以爲稱。」

translations.literal: At the beginning the emperor wished to grant Yue the title Grand Academician; he declined, saying: "Academician originally had no grand title; Emperor Zhongzong in honoring favored great ministers created it—I dare not take it as my title."
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning the emperor wished to grant Yue the title Grand Academician. He declined, saying: "Academician originally had no grand title. Emperor Zhongzong created it to honor favored ministers. I dare not take it as my title."

sentences.zh: 固辭乃免。

translations.literal: He firmly declined and thereby was excused.
translations.idiomatic: He firmly declined and was excused.

sentences.zh: 後宴集賢院，故事，官重者先飲，説曰：「吾聞儒以道相高，不以官閥爲先後。

translations.literal: Later at a banquet in the Collected Worthies Academy, by precedent the higher official drank first; Yue said: "I have heard that Confucians esteem one another by the Way, not by official rank and family gate as before and after.
translations.idiomatic: Later at a banquet in the Collected Worthies Academy, by precedent the higher official drank first. Yue said: "I have heard that Confucians esteem one another by the Way, not by official rank and family status.

sentences.zh: 太宗時修史十九人，長孫無忌以元舅，每宴不肯先舉爵。

translations.literal: In Emperor Taizong's time nineteen men edited history; Zhangsun Wuji as the emperor's uncle by marriage at every banquet would not first raise his cup.
translations.idiomatic: In Emperor Taizong's time nineteen men edited history. Zhangsun Wuji, as the emperor's uncle by marriage, at every banquet refused to raise his cup first.

sentences.zh: 長安中，與修《珠英》，當時學士亦不以品秩爲限。」

translations.literal: In the Chang'an era, when editing the Pearl Splendor, the academicians of that time also did not limit themselves by rank and grade."
translations.idiomatic: In the Chang'an era, when editing the Pearl Splendor, the academicians of that time also did not limit themselves by rank and grade."

sentences.zh: 於是引觴同飲，時伏其有體。

translations.literal: Thereupon he raised his cup and all drank together; the age admired his propriety.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he raised his cup and all drank together. Contemporaries admired his propriety.

sentences.zh: 中書舍人陸堅以學士或非其人，而供擬太厚，無益國家者，議白罷之。

translations.literal: Drafting Secretary Lu Jian held that some academicians might not be the right men, yet their provisions were too generous and of no benefit to the state; he proposed reporting this to have them abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Drafting Secretary Lu Jian held that some academicians might not be the right men, yet their provisions were too generous and of no benefit to the state. He proposed reporting this to have the academy abolished.

sentences.zh: 説聞曰：「古帝王功成，則有奢滿之失，或興池觀，或尚聲色。

translations.literal: Yue heard and said: "Ancient emperors and kings, when their achievement was complete, had the fault of extravagance and fullness—some raised pools and towers, some favored sound and color.
translations.idiomatic: When Yue heard this he said: "Ancient emperors and kings, once their achievement was complete, often fell into extravagance—some raised pools and towers, some favored music and women.

sentences.zh: 今陛下崇儒向道，躬自講論，詳延豪俊，則麗正乃天子禮樂之司，所費細而所益者大。

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty honors Confucianism and turns toward the Way, personally lecturing and discussing, broadly extending invitation to heroic and outstanding men—then Lizheng is the office of the Son of Heaven's ritual and music; what is spent is small and what is gained is great.
translations.idiomatic: Now Your Majesty honors Confucian learning and turns toward the Way, personally lecturing and broadly inviting heroic and outstanding men. The Lizheng Academy is the office of the Son of Heaven's ritual and music. What is spent is small and what is gained is great.

sentences.zh: 陸生之言，蓋未達邪。」

translations.literal: Master Lu's words perhaps have not reached understanding."
translations.idiomatic: Master Lu's words perhaps show a failure of understanding."

sentences.zh: 帝知，遂薄堅。

translations.literal: The emperor understood and therefore treated Jian coldly.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor understood and thereafter treated Jian coldly.

sentences.zh: 説嘗自爲其父碑，帝爲書其額曰：「嗚呼，積善之墓。」

translations.literal: Yue once composed the stele for his father himself; the emperor wrote its title, saying: "Alas, the tomb of accumulated goodness."
translations.idiomatic: Yue once composed the stele for his father himself. The emperor wrote its title: "Alas, the tomb of accumulated goodness."

sentences.zh: 説歿後，帝使就家錄其文，行於世。

translations.literal: After Yue's death the emperor had his writings copied at his home and circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: After Yue's death the emperor had his writings copied at his home and circulated in the world.

sentences.zh: 開元後，宰相不以姓著者，曰燕公云。

translations.literal: After Kaiyuan, for chief ministers who were not known by surname, one said Duke of Yan, and so on.
translations.idiomatic: After the Kaiyuan era, chief ministers who were known not by surname but by enfeoffment were called Duke of Yan, and so on.

sentences.zh: 大暦中，詔配享玄宗廟廷。

translations.literal: In the Dali era an edict ordered him to share sacrifice in Emperor Xuanzong's temple hall.
translations.idiomatic: During the Dali era an edict ordered that he share sacrifice in Emperor Xuanzong's temple hall.

sentences.zh: 子均、垍、埱。

translations.literal: His sons were Jun, Ji, and Chong.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Jun, Ji, and Chong.

sentences.zh: 説子 均均亦能文。

translations.literal: Yue's son Jun was also skilled in writing.
translations.idiomatic: Yue's son Jun was also skilled in writing.

sentences.zh: 自太子通事舍人累遷主爵郎中、中書舍人。

translations.literal: From Communicating Affairs Secretary of the Heir Apparent he was repeatedly promoted to Director of Enfeoffments and Drafting Secretary of the Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: From Communicating Affairs Secretary of the Heir Apparent he rose through the ranks to Director of Enfeoffments and Drafting Secretary of the Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 開元十七年，説授左丞相，校京官考，註均考曰：「父教子忠，古之善訓，王言帝載，尤難以任。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year of Kaiyuan, when Yue was granted Left Chief Minister and reviewed capital officials' evaluations, he noted Jun's evaluation, saying: "Father teaching son loyalty is the good instruction of antiquity; kingly words and imperial records are especially hard to bear.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year of Kaiyuan, when Yue was appointed Left Chief Minister and reviewed capital officials' evaluations, he noted Jun's evaluation: "Father teaching son loyalty is the good instruction of antiquity. Kingly words and imperial records are especially hard to bear.

sentences.zh: 庸以嫌疑，而撓紀綱？

translations.literal: How can one because of suspicion disturb discipline and law?
translations.idiomatic: How can one, because of suspicion, disturb discipline and law?

sentences.zh: 考上下。」

translations.literal: Evaluation: upper and lower."
translations.idiomatic: Evaluation: upper and lower."

sentences.zh: 當時亦不以爲私。

translations.literal: At the time this also was not taken as private favor.
translations.idiomatic: At the time this was not regarded as private favoritism.

sentences.zh: 後襲燕國公，累遷兵部侍郎，以累貶饒、蘇二州刺史。

translations.literal: Later he inherited enfeoffment as Duke of Yan, was repeatedly promoted to Vice Minister of the Board of War, and through accumulated offenses was demoted to prefect of Rao and Su.
translations.idiomatic: Later he inherited enfeoffment as Duke of Yan and rose to Vice Minister of the Board of War, then through accumulated offenses was demoted to prefect of Rao and Su.

sentences.zh: 久之，復爲兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: After a long time he was again made Vice Minister of the Board of War.
translations.idiomatic: After some years he was again appointed Vice Minister of the Board of War.

sentences.zh: 自以己才當輔相，爲李林甫所抑，林甫卒，倚陳希烈，冀得其處。

translations.literal: He considered his own talent fit for chief minister but was suppressed by Li Linfu; when Linfu died he relied on Chen Xilie and hoped to obtain that position.
translations.idiomatic: He considered his own talent fit for chief minister but was suppressed by Li Linfu. When Linfu died he relied on Chen Xilie and hoped to obtain that position.

sentences.zh: 既而楊國忠用事，希烈罷，而均爲刑部尚書。

translations.literal: Before long Yang Guozhong came to power, Xilie was dismissed, and Jun became Minister of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Yang Guozhong came to power. Xilie was dismissed, and Jun became Minister of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 坐垍，貶建安太守。

translations.literal: Through implication in Ji's case he was demoted to grand administrator of Jian'an.
translations.idiomatic: Through implication in Ji's case he was demoted to grand administrator of Jian'an.

sentences.zh: 還，授大理卿，居常觖望不平。

translations.literal: On his return he was appointed Director of the Court of Judicial Review and constantly harbored resentment and discontent.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was appointed Director of the Court of Judicial Review and constantly harbored resentment and discontent.

sentences.zh: 祿山盜國，爲僞中書令。

translations.literal: When Lushan usurped the state, he served as false Chief Minister of the Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: When Lushan usurped the state, Jun served as chief minister of the puppet regime.

sentences.zh: 肅宗反正，兄弟皆論死。

translations.literal: When Emperor Suzong restored correct rule, the brothers were all sentenced to death.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Suzong restored the throne, the brothers were all sentenced to death.

sentences.zh: 房琯聞之，驚曰：「張氏滅矣。」

translations.literal: Fang Guan heard of it and said in alarm: "The Zhang clan is destroyed."
translations.idiomatic: Fang Guan heard of it and said in alarm: "The Zhang clan is destroyed."

sentences.zh: 乃見苗晉卿，營解之。

translations.literal: He then saw Miao Jinqing and worked to secure their release.
translations.idiomatic: He then saw Miao Jinqing and worked to secure their release.

sentences.zh: 帝亦顧説有舊，詔免死，流合浦。

translations.literal: The emperor also considered Yue's old ties and issued an edict sparing their lives; they were banished to Hepu.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also considered Yue's old ties and issued an edict sparing their lives. They were banished to Hepu.

sentences.zh: 建宮初，贈太子少傅。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jianzhong reign he was posthumously given Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Jianzhong reign he was posthumously given Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 子濛，事德宗，爲中書舍人。

translations.literal: His son Meng served Emperor Dezong as Drafting Secretary of the Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: His son Meng served Emperor Dezong as Drafting Secretary of the Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 説子 垍垍尚寧親公主。

translations.literal: Yue's son Ji married Princess Ningqin.
translations.idiomatic: Yue's son Ji married Princess Ningqin.

sentences.zh: 時説居中秉政，均爲舍人，諸父光爲銀青光祿大夫，榮盛冠時。

translations.literal: At that time Yue held the center and wielded government; Jun was drafting secretary; his uncles Guang were Grand Masters of Splendid Happiness with Silver Seal; glory and splendor topped the age.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Yue held power at court. Jun served as drafting secretary, and his uncles Guang held the rank of Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Silver Seal. The family's glory topped the age.

sentences.zh: 玄宗眷垍厚，即禁中置內宅，侍爲文章，珍賜不可數。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong favored Ji thickly, immediately set up an inner residence within the forbidden precincts, attended him in composing literature, and rare gifts could not be counted.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong favored Ji deeply, set up an inner residence for him within the forbidden precincts, had him attend in composing literature, and bestowed rare gifts beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 均供奉翰林，而垍以所賜誇均，均曰：「此婦翁遺婿，非天子賜學士也。」

translations.literal: Jun attended at the Hanlin Academy, while Ji boasted to Jun of what he had been given; Jun said: "This is what a father-in-law left his son-in-law—not what the Son of Heaven gave an academician."
translations.idiomatic: Jun attended at the Hanlin Academy, while Ji boasted to Jun of his gifts. Jun said: "This is what a father-in-law left his son-in-law—not what the Son of Heaven gave an academician."

sentences.zh: 垍嘗爲帝贊禮，舉止都雅，帝悅之。

translations.literal: Ji once assisted the emperor in ritual praise; his bearing was altogether elegant, and the emperor was pleased with him.
translations.idiomatic: Ji once assisted the emperor in ritual praise. His bearing was altogether elegant, and the emperor was pleased with him.

sentences.zh: 因幸內宅，顧垍曰：「希烈辭宰相，孰可代者？」

translations.literal: On an occasion when the emperor visited the inner residence, he turned to Ji and said: "Xilie has resigned as chief minister—who can replace him?"
translations.idiomatic: On an occasion when the emperor visited the inner residence, he turned to Ji and said: "Xilie has resigned as chief minister. Who can replace him?"

sentences.zh: 垍錯愕，未得對。

translations.literal: Ji was startled and confused and could not reply.
translations.idiomatic: Ji was startled and could not reply.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「無易吾婿。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Do not replace my son-in-law."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Do not replace my son-in-law."

sentences.zh: 垍頓首謝。

translations.literal: Ji bowed his head in thanks.
translations.idiomatic: Ji kowtowed in thanks.

sentences.zh: 會貴妃聞，以語國忠，國忠惡之，及希烈罷，薦韋見素代之，垍始怨上。

translations.literal: It happened that the Noble Consort heard and told Guozhong; Guozhong hated him; when Xilie was dismissed, he recommended Wei Jiansu to replace him; Ji then began to resent the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: The Noble Consort heard of this and told Guozhong, who hated Ji. When Xilie was dismissed, Guozhong recommended Wei Jiansu to replace him. Ji then began to resent the emperor.

sentences.zh: 天寶十三載，祿山入朝，以破奚、契丹功，求平章事，國忠曰：「祿山有軍功，然不識字，與之，恐四夷輕漢。」

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Tianbao, Lushan entered court; for his merit in defeating the Xi and Khitan he sought to be Grand Counselor; Guozhong said: "Lushan has military merit, yet he cannot read—if we grant it, I fear the four barbarians will look down on Han."
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year of Tianbao, Lushan entered court. For his merit in defeating the Xi and Khitan he sought to be Grand Counselor. Guozhong said: "Lushan has military merit, yet he cannot read. If we grant it, I fear the four barbarians will look down on the Han."

sentences.zh: 乃止。

translations.literal: Thereupon it was stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the appointment was stopped.

sentences.zh: 及還范陽，詔高力士餞浐坡，力士歸曰：「祿山內郁郁，若知欲相而不行者。」

translations.literal: When he returned to Fanyang, an edict had Gao Lishi see him off at Chan Slope; Lishi returned and said: "Lushan inwardly was depressed, as if knowing he was to be made chief minister but it did not happen."
translations.idiomatic: When Lushan returned to Fanyang, an edict had Gao Lishi see him off at Chan Slope. Lishi reported: "Lushan was inwardly depressed, as if knowing he was to be made chief minister but that it did not happen."

sentences.zh: 帝以語國忠，國忠曰：「所告者必張垍。」

translations.literal: The emperor told this to Guozhong; Guozhong said: "Whoever told him must have been Zhang Ji."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told this to Guozhong. Guozhong said: "Whoever told him must have been Zhang Ji."

sentences.zh: 帝怒，盡逐其兄弟，以均守建安，而垍爲盧溪郡司馬，埱自給事中爲宜春郡司馬。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry and drove out all the brothers; Jun was sent to guard Jian'an, Ji became military aide of Luxi Commandery, and Chong went from Supervising Secretary to military aide of Yichun Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious and drove out all the brothers. Jun was sent to Jian'an, Ji was made military aide of Luxi Commandery, and Chong went from Supervising Secretary to military aide of Yichun Commandery.

sentences.zh: 歳中，還，垍爲太常卿。

translations.literal: Within the year they returned; Ji became Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Within the year they returned. Ji was appointed Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 帝西狩至咸陽，唯韋見素、楊國忠、魏方進從。

translations.literal: When the emperor went west on campaign to Xianyang, only Wei Jiansu, Yang Guozhong, and Wei Fangjin followed.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor fled west to Xianyang, only Wei Jiansu, Yang Guozhong, and Wei Fangjin followed.

sentences.zh: 帝謂力士曰：「若計朝臣當孰至者？」

translations.literal: The emperor said to Lishi: "If we reckon which court ministers ought to arrive, who would come?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said to Lishi: "If we reckon which court ministers ought to arrive, who would come?"

sentences.zh: 力士曰：「張垍兄弟世以恩戚貴，其當即來。

translations.literal: Lishi said: "The Zhang Ji brothers for generations have been noble through imperial kin by marriage—they should come at once.
translations.idiomatic: Lishi said: "The Zhang Ji brothers have for generations been noble through imperial marriage ties. They should come at once.

sentences.zh: 房琯有宰相望，而陛下久不用，又爲祿山所器，此不來矣。」

translations.literal: Fang Guan has the look of a chief minister, yet Your Majesty long did not use him, and moreover Lushan valued him—he will not come."
translations.idiomatic: Fang Guan has the look of a chief minister, yet Your Majesty long did not use him, and Lushan valued him. He will not come."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「未可知也。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "That cannot yet be known."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "That cannot yet be known."

sentences.zh: 後琯至，召見流涕。

translations.literal: Later Guan arrived; summoned to audience he wept.
translations.idiomatic: Later Guan arrived. Summoned to audience, he wept.

sentences.zh: 帝撫勞，且問：「均、垍安在？」

translations.literal: The emperor comforted and rewarded him and also asked: "Where are Jun and Ji?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor comforted and rewarded him and also asked: "Where are Jun and Ji?"

sentences.zh: 琯曰：『臣之西，亦嘗過其家，將與偕來。

translations.literal: Guan said: "When I went west, I also once passed their homes and was about to come together with them.
translations.idiomatic: Guan said: "When I went west, I also passed their homes and was about to come together with them.

sentences.zh: 均曰：「馬不善馳，後當繼行。」

translations.literal: Jun said, 'The horses are not good at galloping—we will follow later.'
translations.idiomatic: Jun said, 'The horses are not good at galloping. We will follow later.'

sentences.zh: 然臣觀之，恐不能從陛下矣。』

translations.literal: Yet as your subject observed, I fear they cannot follow Your Majesty."
translations.idiomatic: Yet as I observed, I fear they cannot follow Your Majesty."

sentences.zh: 帝嗟悵，顧力士曰：「吾豈欲誣人哉？

translations.literal: The emperor sighed in regret and turned to Lishi, saying: "How could I wish to slander people?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sighed in regret and turned to Lishi: "How could I wish to slander people?

sentences.zh: 均等自謂才器亡雙，恨不大用，吾向欲始全之，今非若所料也。」

translations.literal: Jun and the others considered their talent and capacity without peer and resented not being greatly used; I formerly wished at first to preserve them whole—now it is not as you calculated."
translations.idiomatic: Jun and the others considered their talent without peer and resented not being greatly used. I formerly wished to preserve them. Now it is not as you calculated."

sentences.zh: 垍遂與希烈皆相祿山，垍死賊中。

translations.literal: Ji then with Xilie both served Lushan as chief ministers; Ji died among the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Ji then served Lushan as chief minister along with Xilie. Ji died among the rebels.

sentences.zh: 贊贊曰：説於玄宗最有德，及太平用事，納忠惓惓，又圖封禪，發明典章，開元文物彬彬，説力居多。

translations.literal: The appraiser says: Yue toward Emperor Xuanzong had the most virtue; when Princess Taiping wielded power he offered loyal counsel with earnest devotion; he also planned the fengshan, clarified canonical regulations, and in the Kaiyuan era culture and institutions were abundant in refinement—Yue's force was mostly responsible.
translations.idiomatic: The appraiser says: Yue rendered the greatest service to Emperor Xuanzong. When Princess Taiping wielded power he offered loyal counsel with earnest devotion. He planned the fengshan, clarified canonical regulations, and in the Kaiyuan era culture and institutions flourished—Yue's effort was largely responsible.

sentences.zh: 中爲奸人排擯，幾不免，自古功名始終亦幾希，何獨説哉！

translations.literal: Midway he was driven out by treacherous men and nearly did not escape; from antiquity achievement and fame from beginning to end have also been rare—why only speak of Yue!
translations.idiomatic: Midway he was driven out by treacherous men and nearly did not escape. From antiquity achievement and fame maintained from beginning to end have been rare. Why speak only of Yue!

sentences.zh: 至子以利遽敗其家。

translations.literal: As for his sons, through profit they swiftly ruined their house.
translations.idiomatic: As for his sons, through greed they swiftly ruined their house.

sentences.zh: 若瓌、頲再世稱賢宰相，盛矣！

translations.literal: As for Gui and Ting, two generations were called worthy chief ministers—how splendid!
translations.idiomatic: As for Gui and Ting, two generations were called worthy chief ministers. How splendid!
